## SM.6

**The industry seams** (doc 20 §13's SM.6 row): the site clerk's **opening** on the port tick — its own
arm, one receipted `DepositOpen` a fire through the composed `SiteOpener` (no opener grant: the clerk's
identity in `SiteRow.clerk` is its whole authority), one `OreDeposit` per ore-bearing (block, family)
with the family's ore good as the commodity, accessibility 100 and the one-point curve, the reserve the
gross sum of the block's pocket tonnes from the one keyed geology (reading rule v1's pocket evaluation,
read through the warm site ground and never built on the tick), the site's issuer recorded as the
deposit's jurisdiction, then the authored `worked_permille` as a second receipted act — a `transfer_many`
of each pocket's ⌊t × ‰ / 1000⌋ from the block vault to the site's spoil with one cursor row per pocket
that gave a tonne; the readiness line "opening, N of M" until the last deposit exists, the pad closed
meanwhile and open with the layer dark; `tacsim.sites` owning the sixteen block vaults and the spoil;
`OreDeposit.external` and the `ExternalDraws` trait composed at the root, whose 60 s sweep invariant
`initial − pool == Σ drawn` quarantines every deposit of a place on a mismatch; industry's own
`@extract/start` and `@extract/cycle` refusing a surface block (closing SM.5's residual F12 (ii)); the
pocket cursor sidecar `tacsim.pockets:<deposit>` (≤ 64 rows, the lock's one home); mush-inventory's
`transfer_many` staging an endpoint's census once per bundle (SM.3b's round's F3, closed); and the
industry-side tenure machinery — one `TenureRecord` per block place with a `TenureMark`, the epoch
advanced once per block event (lapse, take-over, a seizure that transfers), the cooling rows per
holder, `ClaimRenew` in place, the Abandoned take-over, the seize-transfers-tenure fix on the staff
offer, the composed `JurisdictionAuthority` seam, and the numbers' home `surface::tenure`. No lane,
pack or digest moved (`LANE_VERSION` 11 stands). Built 2026-10-20/21 on main from `354832bf`. Judged
**ship-with-notes**; the lead accepted the four owner-critical defaults (the two typed-state
delegations on the TacSim roster held to reads by a tripwire; the pad open with the layer dark; only
ore-bearing rows open, with SM.7 and SM.10 bound to answer barren and ore-bearing rows alike; block
vaults laid on the next apply for a pre-SM.6 store) and the builder's and fixer's defaults listed
below, and made two hand fixes before the commit. One commit, pushed.

### What landed

1. **One bundle may open any number of new pools at one endpoint** (`crates/mush-inventory/src/record.rs`, `src/pool.rs`). `PoolCensus::checked_add_n(n)`; `apply` refactored into the private `apply_counted(.., CensusWrite::{Write, Staged})`; `InventoryFamilies::transfer_many(txn, from, to, &[(commodity, amount)])` refuses `from == to`, an empty list or a zero amount, more than `MAX_POOLS_PER_ENDPOINT` moves and a repeated commodity (the new `InventoryError::DuplicateCommodity`) before anything is staged, counts the new destination pairs, stages `inventory.census` once with `checked_add_n`, then per move debits, credits (a new pair created without a second census write) and carries the lineage. `transfer` is unchanged. Four tests in `crates/mush-inventory/tests/sm6.rs`.
2. **Held vaults list before machine vaults** (`crates/mush-economy/src/record.rs` `Vault::is_system_owned`, `crates/mush-inventory/src/provider.rs` `collect_live_endpoints`): a person's or an organization's vault is listed before a `System`-owned one, each half in id order, before the 64 truncation. Found by this cut: the lane's 96 block vaults pushed every hull hold made after the lane out of GOD's `@inv/move` and `@market/vendor stock` offers. Pinned by `e7c2.rs` `sm6_a_held_vault_is_listed_before_any_machine_vault`; `commerce.rs` and `voyage.rs` are untouched.
3. **The industry records** (`crates/mush-industry/src/record.rs`). `OreDeposit.external: Option<SmolStr>` (1..=64 bytes of `[a-z0-9_.]`, `MAX_EXTERNAL_BYTES`, `is_external_name`) and `jurisdiction: Option<PrincipalId>`, skipped when `None` and re-checked on the wire, with `with_external`, `with_jurisdiction`, `external()`, `jurisdiction()`; a staff-opened body encodes with exactly its pre-cut keys. `ClaimRecord.epoch: u32`, `discovered_at`, `lapsed_at`, skipped at their defaults, with `is_lapsed()` and the revision-checked post-images `with_term`, `lapsed`, `taken_over` (clears `lapsed_at`, `Uncontested`) and `transferred` (`Uncontested`, term kept). `TenureRecord` per block place — `place`, `epoch`, `since`, `mark: Option<TenureMark>` (`Lapsed` | `Held { holder }`, serde-tagged `kind`), `cooling: Vec<CoolingRow>` — with a strict wire running `check()` (at most `MAX_COOLING_ROWS` 4, one row a holder), `fresh`, `cooling_for` (live while `now < until`; another clock generation counts as live), `on_lapse` (advances unless a lapse opened the epoch; one row a holder, raised only when strictly earlier; rows that ran out pruned on write; the soonest-ending other holder dropped past four) and `on_hold` (advances unless that holder's hold opened it), each `Ok(None)` when nothing changes. New `IndustryRecordError::{External, EpochOverflow, Cooling { max }}`.
4. **The tenure seams and the receipt id** (`crates/mush-industry/src/families.rs`). `IndustryFamilies.tenure` (`industry_tenure`, key `{:010}`, descriptor runs `check`), registered in `module.rs` beside `place_census`. `MAX_RECEIPT_BYTES` 96, `is_receipt` (`[a-z0-9_./-]`), `derive_system_deposit_id(receipt)` hashing `{"class":"deposit.system","receipt"}` on `industry.id.v1` (`InvalidReceipt` otherwise). The seams `tenure`, `renew_claim` (the claim only; `ClaimLapsed`, `ClaimNotLive`, `TermNotLater` also across generations), `lapse_claim` (`lapsed_at = now`; the tenure only on `Some`; a dropped live holder logged at warn), `cooling_until`, `take_over_claim` (`ClaimNotLapsed`, `Cooling { until }`; the index untouched) and `transfer_tenure` (a replay refuses at the revision; checks no authority — its caller gates it). The block-event contract is on the family's doc: the tenure is written only when the transition returns `Some`, so a block's four claims lapse, are taken over or transferred in one bundle or in four with the epoch advancing once; two different tenure changes on one place in one bundle refuse `DuplicateMutation`. A first filing never touches the tenure. New `IndustryError::{InvalidReceipt, ClaimLapsed, ClaimNotLive, TermNotLater, ClaimNotLapsed, Cooling { until }}`, each `ProviderRejected` through `refuse`.
5. **`extraction_authorized` and `file()`** (`crates/mush-industry/src/licence.rs`, `src/provider.rs`): a lapsed claim answers `ClaimExpired` whatever its term (D-20-12); a lapsed exclusive claim still blocks a same-issuer exclusive filing, with the line "that claim has lapsed: take it over".
6. **The seams module** (`crates/mush-industry/src/seams.rs`, re-exported from `lib.rs`): `IndustryHandleCell = Arc<OnceLock<IndustryFamilies>>`; `SystemOpening` (`deny_unknown_fields`, `curve: Vec<CurvePoint>`); `trait SystemOpener { next_opening(&Engine, ObjId) -> Option<SystemOpening> }`; `trait ExternalDraws { drawn(&ModuleCtx, &OreDeposit) -> Option<u64> }`; `trait JurisdictionAuthority { claims(&Engine, &IndustryFamilies, ObjId) -> Vec<ClaimId> }` with the default `ActsForJurisdiction` delegating to `provider::jurisdiction_claims`. `IndustryModule::{with_handle_cell, with_system_opener, with_external_draws, with_jurisdiction_authority, with_state_delegates}` (`crates/mush-industry/src/module.rs`): the delegations are declared first in `register`, the cell is filled right after the families are built and before `provider::register` (a second fill warns), the opener and the authority are threaded into `provider::register`, the draws into both `reconcile` calls.
7. **The system opening and the external refusal** (`crates/mush-industry/src/provider.rs`). For a non-staff actor the `DepositOpen` offer is `opener.next_opening(..)`: fixed `SYSTEM_OPENER` (the actor) and `SYSTEM_OPENINGS` (an object of one row, receipt → `SystemOpening`) with a required `receipt` `Choice` of that key; staff see the offer exactly as before. `open_system` refuses `Unauthorized`/`REFUSED` when the opener is not the actor, the object is not one row, the receipt is not in it, is not a receipt, or the row's own receipt differs; derives the id from the receipt; builds the body with `with_external` and `with_jurisdiction`; `DepositExists` reads "that opening is already made"; the data is `{deposit, receipt, summary, actor, verb}` and never the reserve. `authorized_deposits` skips `external().is_some()`; `start()` and `cycle()` refuse such a body with `REFUSED` (closes SM.5's residual F12 (ii)).
8. **The contest offer's jurisdiction row and the seize-transfers-tenure fix** (`crates/mush-industry/src/provider.rs`). `jurisdiction_claims(engine, families, actor)`: every claim over a `Deposit` whose `jurisdiction()` the actor `acts_for`, sorted, deduped, capped at `MAX_DEPOSIT_CHOICES`. The non-staff `Choice` is the union of `administrable_claims` and the composed authority's row; the fixed `CLAIM_CONTEST_BY`, `CLAIM_CONTEST_STAFF` and `CLAIM_ADMINISTRABLE` are re-checked by `authorize_claim_contest` in `contest()` before anything is read (a missing list refuses outright). The `seized` state's optional `holder` (Text 64) and `discovered` (Integer on `now.clock`) are declared **only on the staff offer** and refused `Unauthorized` for a non-staff invocation; with `holder` the seizure calls `transfer_tenure` with `discovered` or `now` (a later stamp refuses "a discovery cannot postdate the seizure"; `discovered` alone refuses "a discovery stamp goes with a holder"; a holder with another state refuses "a holder goes with a seizure"), the data carrying `claim`, `holder` and `by`, never the stamp; without it the seizure is exactly as before and the epoch does not move. `@claim/seize` is unchanged.
9. **The sweep invariant** (`crates/mush-industry/src/store.rs`). `Quarantine::{DrawsMismatch, DrawsUnanswered, ExternalUnwired}` with runbook lines; `reconcile(.., draws: Option<&dyn ExternalDraws>)` gathers every external body on the deposit walk and, per body, requires `initial_reserve.checked_sub(pool) == Some(drawn)` (an absent pool is 0; an unreadable pool family or a `None` answer is `DrawsUnanswered`; no seam is `ExternalUnwired`), then quarantines every body sharing the place and provider with the same cause; an existing cause wins; `IndustryStore.draws_paged` pages once a boot per body.

The applier submits, credits and computes nothing.

The root creates the `IndustryHandleCell`, hands it to industry on every roster, and on the TacSim roster adds the opener, the draws and `with_state_delegates([tacsim])`; `TacsimRuleset::register` delegates to `industry` when the inventory cell is present.

### Deferred, and why

- **D14, the barren-ness bit (owner-critical, the brief's default taken).** A real site opens only its ore-bearing (block, family) rows (48 on five of the six sites, 64 at Kerwan), and a deposit's existence at its public, receipt-derived id says the block holds that family's ore. Opening all 64 always with barren deposits at a reserve of 0 would need an industry record change and is the owner's; until then SM.7's `+tv/mine [family]` and SM.10's stake must answer a barren and an ore-bearing (block, family) with the same line and fee.
- **D9, the lead's "advanced on open/lapse/seize" (lead ruling 6, read by the brief).** "Open" is epoch 0 ("since the block opened", no write) and "seize" is only the seizure that transfers the claim; a plain seizure with no holder leaves the claim authorizing nobody and the epoch still. Recorded as a reading for the lead to overturn.
- **The seize-with-holder path is staff-only (the fix round's F1, a lead-level narrowing of the brief's 3.5).** The brief declared `holder`/`discovered` on the whole contest offer; as built only the staff offer declares them and `contest()` refuses them for a non-staff actor, because an issuer's or jurisdiction's agent could otherwise rewrite `record.holder` with no title, transferability or pledge check (the split ClaimMove's fold C4 gate). SM.10's contest must carry its challenger as a server-authored row of its own.
- **D8, the jurisdiction carriage SM.10 owes.** `ActsForJurisdiction` lets the Registry suspend a foreign claim at its own sites and nowhere else; it does not by itself carry D-20-12's "inside the player's own acts" (a player does not act for the Registry). SM.10 composes its own `JurisdictionAuthority`, or a server-authored row on its renewal offer, that vouches for a renewing holder's own block's foreign paper. Not a change to D-20-12.
- **D13 closes SM.2's deferral of "the clerk's grant"**: there is no opener grant; the clerk's identity in `SiteRow` is its whole authority, `tacsim.sites` owns the block vaults and the spoil vault, and the block place Things stay the applying actor's.
- **An unresolved issuer opens nothing (lead ruling 7, the fix round's F3, the lead's default).** A deposit is never re-opened, so one opened without its jurisdiction would stay out of the Registry's row for good; the opener offers nothing, the step records `Failed` and pages once, the pad stays closed until the map is repaired.
- **Held vaults before machine vaults in `live_endpoints` (the fix round's F2, a technical default).** The alternative — excluding system-owned vaults from staff lists, or a free-text staff endpoint — was not taken; the 64 cap and `endpoints_truncated` stand as E7c2 fold C12 left them.
- **SM.7 handoffs (reviewer F12):** a pocket may carry two families, so it has two lock homes (one per deposit's cursor) — SM.7 locks both families' rows or accepts per-family locks and says which; a lock row on a pocket with no ore of that family could push a fully drawn 64-row cursor to 65 — SM.7 locks only that family's ore pockets or raises `MAX_CURSOR_ROWS`. `PIT_SEEN` and the pits are derived from the cursor by SM.7/SM.9.
- **SM.10 handoffs:** every tenure event must cover the whole block at one term (the mark records only the last event); the cooling term's `acts_for` half; `block_tenure`'s signature is unchanged and still reads the authored word — SM.10 computes the word from `claims_over(Deposit{..})` plus `IndustryFamilies::tenure(place)` and falls back to it for an unclaimed block; the claim fees are SM.10's (no constant).
- **Tooling gaps left as notes:** the rigs' `stock()` filter also exempts a Failed site line; the work row's endpoints come from the plan, not the deposit; the D10 tripwire's stated blind spots; `read_plan` re-reads on every fire after a capture failure.
- **Deviations the builder declared and I accept:** D2 reads the truth through the public `field_ground` at the same lattice fields and shift; D3's fire-stats check is a count of landed clerk submissions (0 over 20 fires); D7's cold-reboot bound is ≤ 4 fires; the round-trip test checks key sets, not bytes; `TenureMark::Held` is the struct variant `Held { holder }` (an internally tagged enum cannot carry a newtype); `site_step` takes `(ctx, fire, clerk)`, no `PortTickState`; `IndustryRecordError::Cooling` carries `{ max }`; a bad receipt is `InvalidReceipt`.
- **Keyed rigs:** `knowing.rs` and `excursions.rs` open Ahuna before the hop; `geology.rs` and `plumbing.rs` hop to no site and needed no change (both green unedited).

### Residual risks the judge named

- The rigs' `stock()` filter in `excursions.rs`, `knowing.rs`, `sites.rs` and `deposits.rs` exempts every Site line containing `; opening`, which also matches the Failed text (`opening: its ground could not be mapped`), so a keyed rig would not notice a site it does not hop to failing to map; the sites a rig hops to are opened by `open_site`, which asserts Ready, so the failure a test depends on still surfaces.
- The work row's `from`, `to` and `commodity` are authored from the plan row, and the plan-to-deposit cross-check is the reserve of worked rows only (`next_work_row`, `site_step`): a map repair that repoints `SiteRow.vaults[L]` after L opened, or an unworked deposit opened under another table, is not caught at the offer; both fail closed (the transfer refuses, pages, pad stays closed) rather than silently.
- The once-per-block-event epoch rule assumes a block event covers all of a block's claims at one term (`TenureMark` records only the last event): a partial lapse followed by a partial take-over advances the epoch per partial event, so SM.10 must run stake, lapse and take-over over the whole block, which the seam docs and the cut note say.
- The D10 source tripwire is a tripwire, not a proof: it misses a handle passed into a helper under another name, a binding whose right-hand side names no industry source, and braces inside string literals; its self-test proves what it does catch.
- GOD's endpoint `Choice` is still truncated at 64 entries (E7c2 fold C12's pre-existing limit): held vaults now come first, but a world with more than 64 held vaults still loses the later ones from a staff `@inv/move`/`@market/vendor stock` offer, and `endpoints_truncated` still says so.
- `open_system` answers `InvalidRequest` ("an industry action needs a receipt") for an absent `receipt`, not the `Unauthorized` the brief's prose named; every other forged shape (wrong opener, two rows, a receipt not in the rows, a row whose own receipt differs) answers `Unauthorized`/`REFUSED`.
- `read_plan` on a capture failure returns `Failed` without marking the site dark for the boot, so the clerk re-reads the cache on every fire until reboot (one capture a fire); the step pages once and writes nothing.
- The keyed `knowing.rs` suite now opens Ahuna in every test that lands (about 49 port fires each) and runs about 45 s; `ic_slice_loop` 43 s and `ic_buyout_dormancy` 52 s with the 300-fire bound; the Commons takes 97 port fires (about 8 real minutes at 5 s a fire) to open on a live world.
- `collect_live_endpoints` keeps its early `break` on `out.len() > MAX_ENDPOINT_CHOICES` where `out` is now the held half only, so the whole store is scanned whenever fewer than 65 held vaults are takeable; the scan was already bounded by the store and the machine half stops at one past the cap.

### Doc 20 amendments owed

§3.1 (the block places paragraph, "As built (SM.2, SM.3b)"): "SM.6 makes `tacsim.sites` (`SITES_PRINCIPAL`, declared in SM.2) their industry owner" → as built (SM.6, D13) the block place Things stay owned by the applying actor; `tacsim.sites` owns the sixteen block vaults ("{site} block {L} ground", `Container`-backed by the block place, no scope, Active, recorded in `SiteRow.vaults`) and the spoil vault — the deposits' endpoints. The same correction to D-20-2's "owned by the applying actor until SM.6 makes `tacsim.sites` their industry owner" (§14) and §3.4's "`tacsim.sites` is the owner principal of the block places, the deposits' place objects and the spoil vaults".
§3.4: "a per-site site clerk Thing holding the opener grant" → there is no grant: the composed `SiteOpener` admits exactly the live Thing recorded as `SiteRow.clerk` of a latched lane site (D13). "acting through `Fire::as_principal` on the port tick's stock arm" → its own `Arm::Site`, one act a fire, the site clerks sharing `MAX_AGENTS_WORKED_PER_FIRE` 16 with the other arms. "one deposit a fire with the site's server-authored rows as fixed parameters" → one row an offer (the next pending row in plan order), never the whole site (D15). "the readiness line reads a site as 'opening, 41 of 64' until its deposits exist, and the site admits no TV before" → add: with the geology layer dark the line reads Ready ("no deposits while the geology layer is dark") and the pad stays open, since nothing can open (D2); after a boot a keyed site reads "opening: its ground is still being mapped" until the surface tick warms it. "one `OreDeposit` per (block, family)" → per (block, family) whose pockets hold that family's ore; a real site opens up to 64 (48 on five shipped sites, 64 at Kerwan) and a deposit's existence is a barren-ness bit SM.7 and SM.10 must not echo (D14). The worked share: "a pool transfer of that share from the deposit to the site's spoil vault with the drawn tonnes written to the pocket cursor" → per pocket, `⌊t × ‰ / 1000⌋` of every ore pocket of the family, one cursor row per pocket that gave ≥ 1 t (D6; no nearest-first). "`ExternalDraws::drawn(world, deposit) -> Option<u64>`" → `drawn(&self, ctx: &ModuleCtx<'_>, deposit: &OreDeposit) -> Option<u64>` (D11), the typed family readable only through a module context; "a mismatch quarantines the block" → every deposit sharing the place and the `external` name, with the three causes `DrawsMismatch`, `DrawsUnanswered`, `ExternalUnwired`. Add: the two typed-state delegations on the TacSim roster only — industry → tacsim (the port tick and readiness read deposits) and tacsim → industry (the sweep reads `tacsim.pockets`) — each granting write as well, held to reads by `deposits.rs`'s D10 tripwire (D1). Add: the pocket cursor's key text is industry's `{:016x}` id and its pockets are the block's 1..=256 address numbers.
§9.2: "the block's tenure epoch advances" → the tenure is one `TenureRecord` per block place shared by the block's ≤ 4 Deposit-subject claims; its `TenureMark` records what opened the current epoch, so a lapse, a take-over or a transfer advances it once per block event however the claim writes are bundled; epoch 0 is "since the block opened" and a first filing writes nothing; a renewal and a plain seizure do not advance it (D9). "The cooling term: the lapsed holder, and anyone acting for the same principal" → as built the record keeps at most four cooling rows, one per holder (the later `until` kept; the soonest-ending dropped past four and logged); the `acts_for` half is SM.10's; the term is tacsim's `surface::tenure::COOLING_TERM_IC_SECS` (industry's seams take durations as arguments). Add the as-built numbers' home: `crates/tacsim/src/surface/tenure.rs` (`CLAIM_TERM_IC_SECS`, `WORKED_FLOOR_T`, `COOLING_TERM_IC_SECS`, `CONTEST_WINDOW_IC_SECS`, `MAX_LIVE_CLAIMS_PER_ACCOUNT`, `REGISTRAR_WORKED_T`; no fee constant).
§9.4: "the claim transfers … (this needs the seize-transfers-tenure fix, `provider.rs:2171-2200`)" → built as the `seized` state's `holder` and `discovered` parameters (`IndustryFamilies::transfer_tenure`: `Uncontested` under the new holder, `discovered_at` the stamp passed or `now`, the epoch advanced once for the block event), declared on the **staff** offer only in SM.6; SM.10's contest carries its challenger as a server-authored row of its own and passes the heard sounding's real stamp (D10).
§9.6: "The authority for it is a jurisdiction row on the contest offer" → name the seam: a composed `JurisdictionAuthority` whose default `ActsForJurisdiction` (`jurisdiction_claims`) adds every claim over a deposit whose recorded `OreDeposit.jurisdiction` the actor `acts_for`; the Registrar's rule inside the player's own renewal is SM.10's composed authority or server-authored row (D8). Add: every surface deposit records its site's issuer (the Registry) as its jurisdiction at opening, and a site whose issuer has no lane org row opens nothing (fail closed).
§13 SM.6 row, acceptance: "a site opens 64 deposits over 16 places and never attempts a ninth on one" → "a site opens up to 64 deposits over 16 places (64 on an all-families table; only its ore-bearing rows on the real tables) and never attempts a ninth on one"; "the pocket cursor sidecar as the lock's home" stands; add "a seizure that names a holder transfers the tenure (staff-only until SM.10)". The SM.7 row's "Owed first (SM.3b's F3)" → landed in SM.6 as `transfer_many`.
§18, the "10b §3.3 / §15" item → landed (SM.6): the system opener, read handles (`IndustryHandleCell`), `ClaimRenew` in place, the Abandoned take-over, the tenure epoch, `OreDeposit.external`, `ExternalDraws`, the jurisdiction row and the pocket sidecar, as E7 residue closed; the cadence stands as the 5 s port tick.

## SM.4b

**Driving and the map** (doc 20 §13's SM.4 row, split by the lead into SM.4a and SM.4b; this is the
second half): `+tv/drive <target>` with every target kind (a pocket, a field, a block letter, a site
cell, a bearing and metres) as a `Drive` act on SM.3b's one start and one finish — one A* a command
over the site composite at the 65,536-cell budget, the exact path's time and charge from the unit's
speed, the locomotion table and the battery row (a regolith kilometre is exactly 500 IC s and
2,250 cu), the leg frozen for display by an integer Douglas–Peucker at 1, 2, 4 then 8 cells to at most
32 waypoints (refused, never cut, past that; the census over every lane site refuses none), the rig
placed at the leg's end at its due; **the real trip home** for the reserve rule from a per-site home
field built once on the surface tick (a drive to a stand with no way home is refused; a recover is
held only to its own leg's cost, never the 5 % floor, and never reads the battery); `+tv/recover` from
anywhere on the ground as one act carrying its leg to beside the ramp, even with the geology layer
dark (a keyless home field from the atlas terrain); the `site.map` pulled grid feed (the 28-by-28
drive view, the 32-by-32 site view of 80 m cells, the viewer's own readings only, units and the hull,
the public pits from SM.6's cursor, the sounding's transient mark) and `+tv/map [site] [family]` in
line mode with doc 20 §10's legend verbatim (over two lines, being 122 columns), the grid caps raised
to 118 by 32 under the 120-column ruling and `help tui` corrected, the blessed fixtures read alike by
line mode, the TUI's and the web's decoders; the arrival line over SSH; the observer witness; and
`@geology <site> <addr>`. No lane, pack or digest moved. Built 2026-10-21 on main from `60cf3cb0`.
Judged **ship-with-notes**; the lead accepted the owner-critical defaults (the display freeze reading
of §8's 32 waypoints; the way home waived from the 5 % floor; the readings rows without a per-row
drive time; the keyless way home while dark) and the builder's (a recover with no readable battery
row spends nothing for its leg), accepted the crossed 20 ms planning threshold with an atlas cut owed (since landed as cut AP, `74c5801f`),
and made the housekeeping fixes by hand before the commit. One commit, pushed.

### What landed

1. **The drive planner** (`crates/tacsim/src/surface/drive.rs`, new, pure, integers only). `DriveRates` (the unit's tracked `max_speed_cms` 300, the battery row's `drive_cu_per_nominal_cell` 15: no new constant, lead ruling 3), `secs_of_cost`/`cu_of_cost` (ceilings; a regolith kilometre is exactly 500 IC s and 2,250 cu — V2 pinned on flat regolith, rock 1,000/4,500, ice 667/3,000); `Target` (`Pocket`, `Field`, `Block`, `Cell`, `Bearing`) with `parse_target` (`C117`, `c-nw`, `C`, `140,96`, `140, 96`, `ne 300`, `northeast 300`, `ne 300m`, `ne 300 m`), `target_cell` (a pocket's `(4px+2, 4py+2)`, a field's and a block's middle, a bearing's `⌊(m+5)/10⌋` orthogonal or `⌊(100m+707)/1414⌋` diagonal cells) and `target_words`; `drive_leg`: ONE atlas `path` over the site composite at `DRIVE_PATH_BUDGET_CELLS` 65,536 (`Unreachable` and `OverBudget` both `NoPath`), then **the freeze** — an integer Douglas–Peucker (`segment_distance2` as i128 fractions, an explicit stack, ties to the lowest index) at `LEG_TOLERANCE_CELLS` 1, 2, 4 then 8 cells, the first keeping ≤ 32 points winning, refused `Winding { needed }` past 8, never cut; `freeze_always` for a recover (every k-th of the widest's points); `Leg { cells, cost, waypoints, tolerance_cells, secs, cu, metres, heading_mdeg }` with every kept `at_s` the exact path's cumulative seconds. **The home field** (`HomeField`): a multi-source reverse Dijkstra from the ≤ 9 beside-ramp cells over the same `move_cost` in the atlas's neighbour order, each cell's exact least cost home and its first step (`cost_at`, `descend`, self-contained — no composite at descent); `home_cu_to` (0 beside the ramp, `None` with no way home), `home_bound_cost_per_cell` (1,226 on the shipped table: 300 × 141 % × 145 % × 2) and `home_cu_here` (the bound for a stand already occupied), `recover_leg`. Eleven unit tests, including the home field equal to A* on 64 cells of a flat and a noisy grid.\n2. **The freeze census and D15** (`crates/tacsim/tests/driving.rs` `sm4b_the_freeze_census`, `sm4b_the_lane_sites_hold_only_footings_and_passable_craters`): every lane site (the six asserted by name) from the ramp cell to all 64 field middles over the keyless `ground::site_terrain`; every site accepted 64 of 64, all at the 1-cell tolerance, waypoints at most 24 (cap 32), path cells 17–140, identical in debug and release; the lane's cells are regolith, rock or ice only and no feature blocks movement.\n3. **The home cache and its warm** (`crates/tacsim/src/surface/mod.rs`, `ground.rs`, `chart.rs`): `ground::site_terrain` (keyless; `site_composite` factored out of `build_site_ground` as the one shape rule); `GeologyState.{homes, homes_wanted, homes_failed, homes_clock}` bounded at `MAX_HOME_FIELDS` 32 (least recently built dropped); `HomeEntry { built_over: Option<Weak<SiteGround>>, field, built }`; `HomePeek { Dark, Cold, Warm }`; `Peeks { sites, homes }` replacing SM.4a's site-peek map everywhere (`chart::peek_site` takes `&mut Peeks`); `want_home` (a lane site, whatever the layer's state, never a failed one; wants the site too), `hull_home`, `peek_home` built on the pure `home_read(SiteSeen, HeldHome, failed)` — a warm site reads only the field built over that very ground, a dark site only the keyless one, a failed home reads `Dark` whatever the site's peek; `warm_one` works a wanted home when the layer is dark, when nothing is wanted, or when the wanted site is already warm (read from the cache directly so a refused capture warns once), and `warm_one_home` builds over the warm ground (`built_over` it) or from the keyless terrain, skipping a failed or already-warm home, timing each build. Who wants a home: the arrival hook (`composition/sim_routes.rs`), the boot pass (`lib.rs`, every docked programme hull), `act_cmd`/`drive_cmd` on a cold refusal (`want_cold`), the map on a cold site, and a finished drive's tell. ### Deferred, and why

- **D14's STOP (lead ruling 13) — crossed and accepted for this cut, with a follow-up owed.** Release planning corner to corner measured 30.86/33.38 ms (builder), 29.79 ms (fixer), 30.54 ms (gate) against the 20 ms STOP; the budget-exhausted search alone costs the same, so the time is `mush_atlas::physics::path` (per-neighbour string-keyed `table.cost`/`max_slope_pct` lookups, a Chebyshev×100 heuristic against regolith 150). Debug (152 ms against 250) and every home-build figure (33–39 ms release against 50; 190–215 ms debug against 2,000) are under their thresholds. Brief §5 forbids changing the atlas's `path` in this cut and §0 ruling 13 sends a crossed STOP to the lead rather than having the builder improvise; the judge rules it accepted here because the cost sits in the atlas, ordinary drives are a third of the worst case (census median 85–92 cells), and no player load exists pre-launch. Owed: an atlas cut hoisting a per-class cost and slope table out of `path`'s inner loop (and, if the lead prefers, a per-(rig, target, ground) memo so `go` after a preview does not search again — a change to "A* once per command" the cut did not take). D14 asserts only 10× ceilings and so cannot gate the STOP; it is informational until the atlas cut lands.\n- **P4 — the display freeze** (reviewer R1; a technical fork inside §8's own words): the leg is the exact A* path simplified by integer Douglas–Peucker at 1, 2, 4 then 8 cells, time and charge the exact path's, refused only past 32 points at 8 cells; the lane's per-cell terrain makes "corner points" refuse nearly every drive. The census gate held (0 of 64 refused on every site). Owner-critical default, standing until the owner rules.\n- **P6 — the floor is waived for the way home** (lead ruling 5's "cannot afford"): a recover with a leg is refused only when the rig's out-of-bay value cannot cover the leg (`leg_affordable`), never by the 5 % floor, and never reads the battery. Owner-critical default.\n- **Builder decision 3 — a recover with no readable battery row costs nothing**: `rig_rates` reads `cu_per_nominal_cell` 0 without the row (the only figure available without a constant, which lead ruling 3 forbids); D5(d) pins it. A lead default the owner should see beside P6.\n- **P9 — the readings rows drop doc 20 §10's trailing drive time** ("25 s"): no rule gives it without a path per row. Owner-critical default.\n- **P14 — the way home is keyless** (reviewer R3): the home field is built from `site_terrain` when the site reads dark, so only the recover works dark; residual: a terrain edit on a lane site during a dark boot is seen at the next boot.\n- **P13/R2 — no way home is a refusal for a drive** (`NO_WAY_HOME`), the conservative bound kept only for a stand already occupied; latent on today's lane (every slope under 45 %), pinned by the pure tests.\n- **P5 — features are not obstacles** (the atlas's rule): the lane's craters author `movement: false`; D15 fails the day one blocks.\n- **P15 — the sounding mark reads `last` only**: the sounder's next act clears it before the IC hour ends.\n- **P2 — the drive's order rides a RAM slot the offer fixes**, bound to the ordinal and (the fix round) the end cell; a restart loses an unlanded order ("not planned; preview it again").\n- **The legend prints over two lines**: doc 20 §10's legend is 122 columns, past its own 118 cap; the two lines joined are the legend verbatim (`legend_line` holds the whole string). The owner may shorten the legend or accept two lines.\n- **A new crate edge tacsim → mush-ansi** (33 → 34), against the brief's "expected unmoved": lead ruling 7 asks the print to read its rows through `mush_ansi::panel::window_rows`, the TUI's decoder, so line mode and the TUI cannot disagree; mush-ansi is a leaf.\n- **The site view's frame says `extent [32, 32]`, `origin_cell [0, 0]`** and carries a `site.footer` key (the brief named extent [256, 256]); SM.9 reads the site view in 80 m cells.\n- **`+tv` status and `+tv/map` never want a cold home** (the brief's §3.2 list named them); only a cold site is wanted by the map, the home by the arrival hook, the boot pass, `act_cmd`, `drive_cmd` and the arrival's tell. Harmless; SM.9 must not rely on the map warming a home.\n- **Not SM.4b's, untouched**: the TUI screen `q` and the web `FeedScreen` (SM.9), `+tv/plan`, `await tv`, idle return-and-park (SM.11 — `LegShort` must read as "parked where it stands", said in the code), mining and the pit data (SM.7 — `pit_layer` renders the cursor SM.6 built; `lock` absent), the `#` edge (SM.10, a stub), Occator's drones and the cost lane (SM.12), the atlas's `path`, the locomotion table, the tools rows, the lane (v11 unmoved).\n- **Glyph collisions doc 20 §10 chose** (H/O letters against the hull and the crater; slot digits against ore digits): doc amendment candidates for SM.9's screen.\n- **`ActKind::reads_ground` is dead** (no callers after the launches() rewrite); remove or re-document in a later cut.\n- **No world case for `RECOVER_FAR` (unreachable), `RECOVER_DARK` and `NO_WAY_HOME`** on today's lane; pinned by the pure tests only.

### Residual risks the judge named

- D14 STOP crossed: release planning corner to corner 30.5–33.4 ms (debug 152 ms) against the 20 ms STOP; the budget-exhausted search alone costs the same, so it is mush_atlas::physics::path (string-keyed table.cost/max_slope_pct per neighbour, a weak Chebyshev×100 heuristic against regolith 150). Every +tv/drive preview pays it on the world task, unthrottled. Ordinary drives (census median 85–92 cells) cost far less; a follow-up atlas cut (a per-class cost/slope table hoisted out of the inner loop) is owed before SM.12's cost lane.
- A recover whose battery row is unreadable costs 0 cu for its leg home (rig_rates reads cu_per_nominal_cell 0 without the row; builder decision 3, pinned by D5(d)): a free way home whenever tools content is broken — the only figure available without a constant, but the lead should know.
- +tv status and the map never want a cold home (only a cold site); harmless today because the arrival hook, the boot pass, act_cmd and drive_cmd want it, but the brief's §3.2 list named them.
- NO_WAY_HOME, RECOVER_FAR (unreachable) and RECOVER_DARK have no world case on today's lane (every slope under the tracked 45 %, every site terrain captures); they are pinned only by drive.rs's pure tests, the home_read table and the refusal-line unit test.
- The site view's `extent` is [32, 32] with `origin_cell` [0, 0] (the brief said extent [256, 256]); the blessed fixtures carry it, so SM.9's screen must read the site view's extent as 80 m cells.
- Glyph collisions doc 20 §10 itself chose: block letters H and O read as the hull `H` and the crater `O` on the site view; slot digits 1/2 share characters with the ore digits (D12's B has no rig on the ground so its witness is exact). SM.9's screen may want other marks.
- ActKind::reads_ground has no callers left (every `reads_ground() && launches()` became `launches()`); dead public API with a now-misleading doc.
- Stale comments: site_map.rs and its test say the legend is 124 columns (122 chars, 124 bytes); drive.rs's tolerance test says '1.5 cells off' for a 0.5-cell weave; panel.rs's wide-grid comment says 'clamped at the east and north edges' though only x is clamped; the help page's indented legend line is 124 columns, past the 120 floor.
- A started drive that is also untold on the same fire is projected twice in one visit (the tell writes the leg, then project_start writes the same record; the equality check makes the second a no-op).

## SM.7

**Mining** (doc 20 §13's SM.7 row; §6; D-20-9): `+tv/mine [family] [cycles]` (alias `+tv/drill`) and
`+tv/mine stop` — the preview from the operator's own row of the pocket or a public pit, never the
ground (the blind one-cycle core on an unread pocket, its 3 t room the only room line, and a barren
pocket answering byte for byte as an ore-bearing one the operator has not read); the start's gates
(the licence through `licence_gate` with the lapse instant carried as a fixed parameter, then
`extraction_authorized` over the block's own claims, the commons and open-ground rules; the hopper's
and the hold's unreserved room in every measure; the run's charge and its trip home reserved); the
**run** in the record's cycle slot beside the act slot on SM.3b's one start action, locking the
pocket's cursor rows, **each cycle landing at its own due through the one finish** (the transfer of
the family's ore good from the block vault to the hopper, the cursor's `drawn_t`, the receipt
`(tv, run ordinal, k)`, that cycle's charge spent, the next cycle re-armed or the run closed with its
locks released); the licence, the tenure and the lease judged for the NEXT cycle, never the running
one, never the way home; the core's R2 row with `Instrument::Core` and `PIT_SEEN`; the cycle line over
SSH; the `tacsim:mined:{site}` ring; terrain-scaled pace and the drill row's yield (lean 1, fair 2,
rich 3 t a cycle). No lane, pack or digest moved. Built 2026-10-21 on main from `d367bf3b` (with the
Draft 0.7 docs commit `a0030f71` landing under the run). Judged **ship-with-notes**; the lead accepted
the six owner-critical defaults (`stop` without `go`; no mining under a forfeit or ended lease; a
public pit as one preview clause; an authored held block refusing before SM.10; the blind core's
default family; the texts as written) and ran a fix round before the commit. One commit, pushed.

### What landed

1. **The run in the record** (`crates/tacsim/src/surface/excursion.rs`). `ActKind::Mine` (word `mine`; a `Mine` act never exists — `RigRecord::check` refuses one); `RefusedCode::Unworked`; `RigRecord.run: Option<Run>` — the **cycle slot** beside the act slot (serde default, skipped when `None`, schema 1 stands) with `Run { ordinal, operator, hull, slot, site, body, stand, pocket, number, letter, family, deposit, good, source, hopper, cycles, k, secs, cost_cu, reserve_t, class_t, pocket_t, blind, stop, lapses_ic, lock_rows, due_ic, reserved_cu }`, `Run::outstanding_t`, `MAX_RUN_CYCLES` 8, `MAX_LOCK_ROWS` 2, `LockRow`; `check` holds every bound (a scan or a sounding started later may share the rig with a run, nothing else); `Outcome.mined: Option<Mined>` with `RunEnd { Done, WorkedOut, Stopped, Licence { why: LicenceEnd }, Claimed, Lease { forfeit }, Refused }` and `LicenceEnd` (the standing, never prose); `reserved_total` = the act's plus the run's remaining reservation, saturating; `TvRec.told_cycle` and `TvRec.run: Option<Box<RunView>>` (`RunView { ordinal, k, cycles, due_ic }` — no pocket, family or class).

### Deferred, and why

- **R7 — `+tv/mine stop` commits with no `go`** (lead ruling 8; an owner-critical default standing until the owner rules): a control on a committed run that only drops future cycles at no cost, like `+tv/quiet`'s preference, not an act with a preview.
- **R15 — a forfeit or ended lease bars mining at the start and stops the next cycle, never recover, drive or dump** (the lead's/planner's owner-critical default): `lease_gate` is one rule shared with the launch; the way home is never barred.
- **R16 — a public pit shapes the blind preview by one clause, never a refusal** (owner-critical default): `PIT_WORKED`/`PIT_WORKED_OUT` read the one `pit_at` rule the map folds through; a refusal on `V` would deny ore a two-family pocket still holds.
- **R5 — an authored held block with no live claim refuses `MINE_CLAIMED`** until SM.10 seeds Occator's claims (M9 pins Occator Rim's F); commons never reads claims; a holder-less held block reads open as `block_tenure` counts it.
- **R6 — the blind family default** is the named family, else the richest family of the operator's own R1 row of the field, else metals (owner-critical default; M19(c) pins it).
- **R9 — rights for the next cycle**: the licence is judged at the cycle's own due against the lapse instant read at landing, whether read in force or already lapsed (the fixer narrowed the brief's step 7 for `Lapsed` only, so a late landing after a restart decides as the uninterrupted world — M12b); the tenure and the lease are the offer's verdict at landing (claims carry no instant to replay) — residual; R9's converse (a renewal during the gap reads in force) is the same residual.
- **R20 — a claim past its term that nothing lapsed is open ground** until SM.10's lapse machinery (M8(d) pins it); an uncomparable term counts as live (fail closed); any contest state bars the block, its holder included.
- **Every new player-facing text** (the `MINE_*`, `CYCLE_*`, `RUN_*`, `CORED`, `FIT_*`, `PIT_*`, `RUN_LINE`/`CORE_LINE` constants in `port/tv.rs`) is the planner's wording for the owner to see; doc 20's verbatim lines (§1's cycle line, "That block is under claim.", "Another rig is working that pocket.", §6's no-fit line with the slot, the blind sentence and its 3 t room clause) are pinned byte for byte. `MINE_PREVIEW`'s `{cycles} cycles` became `{cycles}` filled from `ONE_CYCLE`/`SOME_CYCLES` (one cycle reads "1 cycle").
- **The lead's 2 (existence-hiding), 3 (the lock per cursor row, both families, only rows that exist), 4 (the tools table's yield and pace; one `hold_unreserved`), 6 (conservation is the transfer; the receipt over `(tv, ordinal, k)` — R2 — since doc 20's `(deposit, pocket, k)` collides on a second run of the pocket), 7 (`Instrument::Core`, `PIT_SEEN`; no map code beyond the behaviour-free `pit_at` factoring) were taken as written.
- **The start's prepare does not re-run `lease_gate`** (the brief's 3.4 listed it): the prepare holds no world; the lease, the tenure and the plan are the offer's re-plan at landing (`mine_fixed`), which the world task runs in the same synchronous step. Recorded as a deviation, not a decision.
- **`capacity::fits_in` was not exposed**; `mine::fits` restates the per-measure rule (an unnamed measure is unlimited). Deviation from 3.5, undeclared by the builder.
- **No `age_licence_for_tests` helper**: the lapse uses `reboot_editing` of `tacsim:licence:<account>` (`expires_ic`, `grace_secs` 0 — the restart-edit seam driving.rs and excursions.rs use); `Other` edits the document's `holder`; `Unlicensed` swaps the pilot's account in the `MapOracle`; `Suspended` uses `mush_economy::set_account_status(.., Frozen)`.
- **M8's `LICENCE_OTHER` case is the holder edit, not a second character**; M8(b)'s recover asserts a landed `Done`, not the preview text; M13 parks A's rig 40 cells away (its doc comment says one).
- **M15's retell** is simulated by rebooting with the projection's `told_cycle` set to 0; the D24 order (the ring written only after the projection landed) is by construction, not exercised.
- **The harness ledger** (`tests/mining.rs`): a coordinator-level HIT cannot be built inside tacsim's tests (mush-server depends on tacsim), so `Rig.ledger` mirrors `ActionCoordinator::command_ingress`'s digest inputs (`ledger_identity`); the prepare-level races are reachable only by splitting `resolve` and `prepare` (in production the guards are defence-in-depth behind the offer's re-plan).
- **Staff placement (`with_ctx` + `mush_sim::place`) does not survive a restart**: tests that reboot re-place the rig; M12 drives for real.
- **The start moves an in-bay charge out of the bay** before writing the run (a staff-placed rig), so cycles settle with `settle_spent_out_of_bay` alone.
- **`Refusal::Licence { line }`** carries the formatted `standing_line` (a refusal is RAM-only); `RunEnd` still stores the standing.
- **`MinePlan.outstanding` is in tonnes**, weighed per measure inside `hold_unreserved`.
- **Boxed for clippy**: `ActOrder::Mine(Box<MineOrder>)`, `TvRec.run: Option<Box<RunView>>` (the wire form is the view's).
- **A2's soak is the arithmetic half** (`cycle_yield`, `pocket_yields`, `cursor_after`, the caps over a modelled pool); the bundle's conservation is M2's sweep.
- **Not built here**: `+tv/unload` and `HOPPER_LOADED`'s remedy (SM.8; §13's "unloads" acceptance is SM.8's), the map's `lock`/run field and `tv.status` keyframe and the two-family `V` rule (SM.9: a pocket worked out in one family and untouched in the other reads `V` on every map), `+claim` (SM.10), `+tv/plan` (SM.11), the mill and the write-count measurement (SM.12; §11's ≤ 8 writes a completion holds by construction only). `docs/help/mining.md` is complete through beat 8.
- **Residuals handed on** (see the risks): `lock_live` without the block letter; `rig_flight` ignoring a run; a Dark tenure told as `MINE_CLAIMED`; the projection's run only from the first due; stale `ActOrders` re-planned on later offers; hold-admitting writers outside mining ignoring the reservation (SM.8/market); the body caps on a read run after a mid-run `+tv/forget`.

### Residual risks the judge named

- `mine::lock_live` matches a run's `(site, number)` but not its block letter: a stale lock on C17 reads live while a staff-re-created record's run of the same ordinal drills F17 (self-healing when that run ends; a one-line fix is to require `run.letter` or `run.lock_rows.contains`).
- `port::tv::rig_flight` does not read `record.run`: a drilling rig with its excursion open answers departure with `TV_OUT` naming `+tv/<n> recover`, which then refuses `MINE_RUNNING` (two hops to `mine stop`); a staff-placed rig with a run and no excursion reads Idle to the return/repossession checks (a test seam, not a play path).
- A tenure read that fails at landing (`TenureBar::Dark`: unresolved issuer, unreadable deposit or claim, or a missing site def) stops the run as `RunEnd::Claimed` and the pilot hears "That block is under claim." — fails closed, but the public line is false for a dark read.
- The projection `tacsim:tv:<tv>` shows `run` only from the first cycle's due (or a tell): for the whole first cycle a feed consumer sees the rig idle while it drills; `+tv` reads the record and is right. SM.9's screen should project the run at the start's first fire (P8's `started` shape).
- A landed mine order is never cleared from `ActOrders`, so every later start offer for that actor re-runs `mine_plan` for the rig (refused `mine_changed`/`mine_running` and discarded): cost and stray warn logs only.
- The hold's unreserved room is read by the mining plan and the map only; market purchases and other hold writers still admit against `limit − load`, so cargo bought mid-run can leave a hopper the hold cannot take — SM.8's unload must say what happens, or hold-admitting writers must read `hold_unreserved`.
- The start's prepare does not re-run `lease_gate`; a forfeit between `go` and landing is refused by the offer's re-plan (`mine_fixed`), which the world task runs in the same synchronous step — defence-in-depth only if offers are ever fixed earlier.
- `mine::fits` restates `capacity::fits_in`'s per-measure rule instead of exposing it (an unnamed measure is unlimited in both today); the two can drift.
- A read run after a mid-run `+tv/forget` re-creates the operator's chart row at the core without the body caps (checked at the start only for a blind core); `row.check()` still bounds the record.
- A cycle finish that was submitted and merely dropped (never refused) is recorded `Unworked` on the retry and ends the run — the brief's two-pass design (the dump's `SpoilGone` precedent), pinned by M18(b).
- R9's converse: a licence renewed between a cycle's due and a late landing reads in force; tenure and the lease are judged at landing (claims carry no instant to replay).
- Two comments are inaccurate: state-slot-owners' mining.rs reason says the `LICENCE_OTHER` case is a second character (the test edits the licence document's holder), and M13's doc comment says A's rig is parked one cell away (the code parks it 40 cells away).
- `sm7_the_pit_bit_reads_as_sounded` does not assert `pocket_text` gives the R2 text (the brief asked for it); `pocket_sounded`/`row_reads_pocket` are asserted.
- `sm7_ten_thousand_cycles_conserve` is A2's arithmetic half only; the real bundle's conservation is M2's sweep after a read run, a blind ore core and a blind barren core.
- `--test mining` runs about 60 s wall (21 tests; the slowest, M12, a little over 60 s inside the binary).

### The lead's fix round (before the commit)

a drilling rig is busy to the departure gate (`TV_BUSY` "drilling C117" with the stop as the remedy), the lease return and the repossession (`RigFlight::Drilling`, read after an act and before an open excursion), a dark registry read ends the run as `RunEnd::Dark` with its own line and never "That block is under claim." (precedence Refused > WorkedOut > Stopped > Dark > Licence > Claimed > Lease > Done), the projection shows a run from the first fire after its start lands, a stale lock is matched by its row (deposit and pocket) and not only its number, a landed mine order is skipped by the offer without a re-plan and pruned by the tick's complete scan, `mine::fits` calls `capacity::fits_in` (now `pub(crate)`), two comments were corrected and the pit bit's text and its tier-less refusal are asserted.

The round was interrupted by a session restart after its fixer, reviewer and re-fixer had finished; it was resumed with those three cached and only the gate re-run, over a tree that by then carried fourteen of the owner's pixel-cockpit and dev2 commits (held back from the push by the owner's ruling). The lead's rulings on the round's review (verdict ship; the one should-fix — `bay_gate`'s doc — re-fixed in the round):

- **N1, residual.** `RIG_BUSY`'s "done {when}" for a drilling rig names the running cycle's due, not the run's end (a run re-arms past it unless stopped); carrying `k` and `cycles` into `RigFlight::Drilling` so the words read "drilling C117, cycle 2 of 4" is a one-line improvement for the next cut that touches `tv.rs`.
- **N2, for the owner.** `RUN_DARK` (" The registry cannot be read here; the run at {addr} ends with this cycle.") is new player-facing text in the dark-layer voice rather than `RUN_RIGHTS`'s end-clause shape (" Rig {n} stops drilling {addr}: …"); the owner rules on the wording at the cut note.
- **N3, residual.** M21 makes the read dark by dropping the issuer org; the `DarkCause::{Deposit, Claims}` arms are mapped but not exercised by a world test, and the once-only page is not asserted (no log-capture helper in `mining.rs`).
- **N4, confirmed.** The brief's rule stands: `RunView` carries no pocket, family, yield or class; SM.9's screen takes the pocket and family from the record-backed reads (`+tv`, `site.map`), and its planner's choice to add the operator's own address and good to the view is recorded there as a deviation for the lead.
- **N5, N6, N7, residuals.** A genuinely overtaken mine start answers "not planned" where a drive answers "orders moved on"; `shown_run_of` compares only `(ordinal, k)`, so a staff re-creation that resets ordinals could match a stale projection for one fire; the offer reads every rig's record for `next_ordinal` and the prune builds a map on every complete fire — compute both only when a mine order exists.
- **Pins moved by the round:** none re-blessed; `state-slot-owners.toml`'s `mining.rs` reason text only. Two server-only wires changed with no live data: `RightsVerdict.tenure` (a `TenureRead`, was a bool) in the finish's fixed parameters, and `RunEnd` gained `Dark { why }`.
- **Gate:** the cut's own steps all green (tacsim 3,077 over 60 binaries, workspace 8,511, mush-bot 717, contract tests, clippy); `cargo fmt --check` and the strict rustdoc fail only in the owner's `mush-pixel` and TUI pixel files (CRLF in the working tree; a public doc linking a private item), proven by `git log` on each file and by a clean `--exclude mush-pixel` doc run; one load flake (`mushd --test arena_story`) passed alone twice.

Anything else is stale and can be taken. Both callers in crates/tacsim/src/surface/act.rs were updated: `mine_plan` builds `LockRow { deposit: id, pocket: number }` for each family's cursor, and `pocket_taken` passes its own row and no longer takes the unused `number`. **The round's review.** I reviewed the fix-round delta from tree 67fb5adc to tree 6193d3d17304d7faf0f1ac6b9556600fef94a354, which I computed with a scratch index; the real index was not touched. The delta is 11 files, +864/−131. All eight items on the lead's list are done and done correctly, and each has a real test. I found no must-fix.

What each item now does:
1. `lock_live` matches the locked row itself (deposit and pocket) through `run.lock_rows.contains(row)`. That is exactly the set of rows the start locks (act.rs:3402-3411, 5229), so a live run can never read as stale.
2. `RigFlight::Drilling` sits between the act arm and the excursion arm. The bay gate, `plan_return` step 11 and `repossess` (through `rig_out_or_busy`) all treat a run as busy. M20 tests the departure exactly; the new excursions test covers return and go, the revoke holding, and a control in which the revoke goes through once the run is cleared.
3. `RunEnd::Dark` and `DarkCause` follow the precedence the lead asked for. A missing site definition now maps to Dark, never Claimed. The start's dark refusal is unchanged. The page fires once, gated on the projection being written. M21 shows the running cycle yields, `RUN_DARK` is told once, `MINE_CLAIMED` is never heard, and nothing moves afterwards.
4. A started run becomes a candidate, ordered by `due_ic − secs`, and `project_run` or `project_start` writes it on the first fire. M20 checks this before the first due with no finish queued; a unit test covers the candidate rules.
5. The offer drops an order whose ordinal is not the next one, quietly and without re-planning, and the tick prunes such orders only on a complete scan. M20's forged start tells the two behaviours apart (`unplanned` against `mine_running`), and the slot is empty after one fire.
6. `mine::fits` now calls `capacity::fits_in`, now `pub(crate)`, over the measures the room names. It differs only for a per-unit figure of 0, and goods validation already refuses that (goods.rs:287, 395).
7. Both comments now match the code.
8. The chart test pins the cored byte and that `check` refuses a byte with `PIT_SEEN` and no tier. M1 pins the R2 text through `pocket_reading` (`pocket_text` returns either `NO_READING` or the R2 row, so `starts_with(addr) && != NO_READING` is the R2 form).

Pins and assertions: nothing was weakened. The rewritten tests keep every old case and add new ones. The tick tests only gained a `|_| None` argument, plus a projection that already shows the run in the take-turns test, so its pinned values are unchanged. No content, lane or fixture pin moved, and no RNG was added. The only truth the new player text carries is the operator's own pocket address, which `MINE_RUNNING` already tells. `RunView` still carries no pocket, family or class.

One should-fix: several doc comments still describe only an act in flight. The notes below are mostly wording calls for the owner or lead, plus small efficiency and robustness follow-ups.

- **S1** (should-fix): bay_gate's doc (voyage.rs:2448-2455) still lists the refusals as `TV_BUSY` "with an act in flight; else, with the hull on a site's pad, TV_OUT (... a rig a staff move left in the bay with its excursion open reads TV_OUT ...)". Two const docs are equally stale: TV_BUSY (voyage.rs:409, "a rig mid-act") and RIG_BUSY (tv.rs:253, "An act in flight"). Both are now also used for a run, with RUN_STOP_REMEDY appended. Also, the edited `rig_out_or_busy` doc line at tv.rs:3536 runs to 118 columns. Item 7 of this same round existed because comments had drifted from the code.
- **N1** (note): tv.rs:3113-3121: the lease return for a drilling rig reads `RIG_BUSY` ("Rig {n} is {doing}: done {when}.") with `{when}` set to `run.due_ic`, which is the running cycle's due, not the run's end. The run re-arms past that instant unless it is stopped, so "Rig 1 is drilling C117: done <time>." reads as if the rig will be free then. The appended RUN_STOP_REMEDY ("ends the run after this cycle") only implies the cycle. `MINE_RUNNING` avoids this by saying "cycle {k} of {cycles}: done {when}". The lead's own spec put `due_ic` in `Drilling`, so this is the lead's or owner's call.
- **N2** (note): tv.rs:528-529 `RUN_DARK = " The registry cannot be read here; the run at {addr} ends with this cycle."`. It is new player-facing text, and the fixer flagged it. It departs from the end-clause voice of `RUN_RIGHTS` (" Rig {n} stops drilling {addr}: {line}"), which tells the other right-based ends. It also departs from the dark-layer voice used elsewhere ("... cannot be read right now; nothing changes.": TV_DARK, CHART_UNREAD). "here" is ambiguous: the line is told to an operator who may be offline or elsewhere.
- **N3** (note): M21 (mining.rs:4080-4163) makes the read dark by dropping the issuer org (`drop_lane_org_for_tests`). The lead asked for a broken deposit or claim read. As a result, the `DarkCause::Deposit` and `DarkCause::Claims` mappings (act.rs:3018-3027) are not exercised by any test, and nothing asserts the `tracing::error` page in tick.rs:1128-1149, because no log capture exists. The deviation is documented, and the issuer path is a real Dark cause that goes through the same `RunEnd::Dark` code, so the player-facing behaviour is covered.
- **N4** (note): Item 4 asked for the P8 `started` shape "pocket, family, k, cycles, the next due". The fixer kept `RunView { ordinal, k, cycles, due_ic }` (excursion.rs:1483-1489) because the binding SM.7 brief says (brief.md:167) "no pocket, family, yield or class — the projection decides nothing and shows nothing a blind core could leak". I agree with following the brief. M20 asserts the as-built shape.
- **N5** (note): The ordinal filter in `mine_fixed` (act.rs:4069-4074) changes what a genuinely overtaken mine start answers. Because the prepare checks the fixed plan's refusal (act.rs:4676-4681) before `start_run`'s ordinal check (act.rs:5103-5105), a start whose order another act overtook now answers "that act was not planned; preview it again" (`unplanned`). Before this round it re-planned and ended in `mine_running`, busy, or "that rig's orders moved on". A stale drive start still answers "that rig's orders moved on" (driving.rs D9). The order was planned, so "not planned" is slightly off, though the remedy ("preview it again") is right. This is a race path (two `go`s close together).
- **N6** (note): `shown_run_of` (tick.rs:679-689) and the started filter (tick.rs:407-411) compare only `(ordinal, k)`. After a staff re-creation through `RigRecord::fresh`, which resets the ordinal (the very case item 1 deals with), a new run can match a stale projection's `(ordinal, k)` while having a different `due_ic`. In that case it is not projected until its first due. SM.4b's `shown` has the same weakness.
- **N7** (note): The start offer reads the excursion record for every rig on every offer, whether or not the rig has a mine order (`next_ordinal`, act.rs:4541-4547). `prune_mine_orders` (act.rs:2523-2537) builds a BTreeMap over every scanned record on every complete fire (tick.rs:472-474), even when `ActOrders` holds no mine order. Both are small, but they sit on hot paths that the residual this round fixes was itself about (offer cost).

### Doc 20 amendments owed

- §6 "The start is an authoritative submission as the operator (`tacsim_surface_mine`)": as built (SM.7) it is `act = mine` on `tacsim_surface_act` with `+tv/mine stop` as `act = mine_stop` (no third action; SM.3b's decision 25 stands); the start's prepare writes the run into the record's **cycle slot** (`RigRecord.run`) beside the act slot and locks the pocket's cursor rows in one bundle; the preview is the command's `mine_plan`, re-planned by the offer at landing and required equal (`MINE_CHANGED`), so `go` commits exactly the preview or nothing.
- §6 "a receipt keyed `(deposit, pocket, k)` as the replay guard": as built the receipt is the finish's idempotency key `tacsim.surface/{tv}/{ordinal}/cycle/{k}` over `(tv, run ordinal, k)` — the run froze its deposit and pocket, and a second run of the same pocket restarts `k`; the prepare's `(ordinal, k)` check is the second guard.
- §6 "`capacity::admits` over the hopper compartment and over the hull's hold plan with the hold's unreserved room": as built `mine::fit` names the count that fits in every measure (mass and packed volume, §19 item 1's promise held by volume too) against the hopper's room and `port::ship::hold_unreserved` — the one function the map's `hold.room_t` reads, now counting every outstanding cycle of every rig of the hull; the blind room is `mine::blind_room_t` (the richest yield of the drill row, 3 today), derived, never a constant.
- §6 "Two rigs on one pocket: the lock refuses the second": as built the lock is one cursor row per family with ore (at most two), and the start also refuses when any other rig's run record stands on the pocket, so an all-barren pocket (which has no row) refuses "Another rig is working that pocket." byte-identically (R4); a lock whose holder's record has no run of that ordinal on that pocket is stale and taken.
- §6 "the preview … from the operator's own R2 row of the pocket, or a public pit": as built the public pit adds one clause to the blind preview (`PIT_WORKED` / `PIT_WORKED_OUT`, the map's own `pit_at` rule) and never refuses nor changes the run (R16, an owner-critical default the lead accepted, standing until the owner rules); a read pocket's preview prints each cycle's tonnes from the cursor's remainder.
- §6 "`+tv/mine stop` lets the running cycle complete": as built it is committed without `go` (R7, an owner-critical default the lead accepted, standing until the owner rules).
- §6 "A bounded per-site ring publishes the cycle as the fact `tacsim.surface.mined`": as built `tacsim:mined:{site}` (`MinedRing`, 64 facts, inserted in `(at_ic, tv, ordinal, k)` order, never doubled), written by the tick's tell after the projection's write, only for a cycle that moved ≥ 1 t (a barren core is never published), read by nothing yet.
- §6 "the chart's R2 row": as built `chart::write_core` writes the pocket's R2 with `PIT_SEEN`, provenance `Local { Core, at: due_ic, Hand }` (`Instrument::Core`), creating the operator's row with the run's body when they have none; a core never feeds the same-cell repeat rule.
- §8 "the current cycle `{pocket, family, k, cycles, yield}` and the locked pocket's address": as built `Run` on the `RigRecord` also freezes the site, body, stand, number and letter, the deposit, the good, the block vault and hopper endpoints, `secs`, `cost_cu`, `reserve_t`, the true `class_t`/`pocket_t` (never projected), `stop`, `lapses_ic`, the lock rows, `due_ic` and the remaining `reserved_cu`; `reserved_total` is the act's plus the run's; only a scan or a sounding started later may share the rig.
- §8 "A licence that lapses or a claim that is lost stops the next cycle": as built the licence is judged at the next cycle's own due against the lapse instant read at landing, whether the standing reads in force or already lapsed (R9, restart-equivalent); the tenure and the lease are the offer's verdict at landing; **a forfeit or ended lease also stops the next cycle** and bars a start (R15, an owner-critical default the lead accepted, standing until the owner rules); the running cycle always yields; a refused cycle (`Moved`, `Unworked`) spends nothing, moves nothing and closes the run with its locks released; the end's precedence is `Refused > WorkedOut > Stopped > Licence > Claimed > Lease > Done`.
- §8 "the post-image after a restart equals an uninterrupted run (an acceptance test)": as built pinned for a run by M12 and M12b.
- §3.4 "the lock's one home is the sidecar row … a second rig's start reads it in one `get`": as built the start reads the row's lock and the other rigs' run records (R4), and the row is locked with `PocketLock { tv, ordinal }`, released at the close, a row neither drawn nor locked removed.
- §5 (the pocket byte): as built `PIT_SEEN` is written by the core and reads as sounded; the mine preview's blind default family is the named one, else the richest of the operator's own R1 row of the field, else metals (R6, an owner-critical default).
- §9.2/§13 (tenure before SM.10): as built an authored **held** block with no live claim refuses "That block is under claim." (R5) until SM.10 seeds Occator's claims; a claim past its term that nothing lapsed reads as open ground (R20, residual for SM.10); an uncomparable term counts as live; any contest state bars its holder too.
- §10 the `+tv` status: as built gains `RUN_LINE` / `CORE_LINE` under a drilling rig, and `+tv[/<n>]/mine [family] [cycles] [go]` (alias `drill`) and `+tv[/<n>]/mine stop` on `TV_USAGE`/`TV_HELP`.
- §11 Tick row "≤ 8 writes a completion": as built by construction only (the record, at most two cursors, the chart; the ring is the tick's own document), unmeasured until SM.12.
- §11 Caps row: add — a run at most eight cycles, two lock rows, a mined ring of 64 facts a site.
- §13 SM.7 row: mark **landed**; the "unloads" half of "recovers and unloads" is SM.8's; add the as-built notes above and the debts handed on (the two-family `V` and the run on the projection to SM.9; hold-admitting writers reading `hold_unreserved` to SM.8; the lapse of term-expired claims to SM.10; the write-count measurement to SM.12).
- §14 D-20-9: add "**As built (SM.7):** the run in the record's cycle slot on the one start action, each cycle keyed per cycle; the lock per family row plus the run-record check; the blind room derived from the drill row; `stop` without `go`, the public pit as one clause, the blind family from the operator's own R1 row, and the lease bar on mining (the lead's owner-critical defaults, standing until the owner rules)". D-20-11: add the cycle slot and "rights judged at the next cycle's due (the licence) and at landing (tenure, lease)". D-20-5: add "every cycle `InventoryFamilies::transfer` from the block vault to the hopper with the cursor's `drawn_t` in the same bundle; `ExternalDraws` green on M2's sweep".
