## AP

**The atlas path search's cost** (an engine cut in `mush-atlas` with no doc 20 §13 row of its own,
owed by SM.4b's crossed 20 ms planning threshold and recorded on §13's SM.12 row and beside SM.7's):
`path` resolves its locomotion's rows once per search into a dense per-class row
(`mush_atlas::LocomotionCosts`, eighteen slots by `TerrainClass::code()`, one slope limit and one
climb, sharing one private step rule with `move_cost` so every other caller answers bit for bit) and
steers by the octile distance priced at the cheapest passable class present on the surface —
admissible and consistent, so it returns the least cost, unchanged for every row whose passable
classes all cost at least 100 (the drive's tracked row among them); the home field reads the same
row; every path cost on every lane site is proven equal against a plain Dijkstra over `move_cost`;
SM.4b's planner measurement becomes a release gate on the minimum of five runs (planning ≤ 10 ms,
the home field and the exhausted flood ≤ 20 ms), the debug pair asserting only under
`TACSIM_ASSERT=1`. On Ahuna Flank in release, corner-to-corner planning went from 29 ms to 3.3 ms,
the home field from 33 ms to 7 ms and the exhausted flood from 29 ms to 8 ms. No lane, pack or digest
moved; nothing player-facing changed beyond one equal-cost tie on Ahuna freezing to a different
waypoint count. Built 2026-10-21 on this checkout's local main from `0fdd2056` (SM.7 over the
owner's held-back commits) and landed by cherry-pick onto origin/main. Judged **ship-with-notes**;
the lead accepted the one owner-critical default (the debug timings never gate the push-triggered
CI shard, per D-H-8 and D-16-19) and landed it without a fix round. One commit, pushed.

### What landed

1. **One step rule, two lookups** (`crates/mush-atlas/src/physics.rs`). The arithmetic after `move_cost`'s two table walks — the rise, the climb onto built ground within the locomotion's climb, the slope (0 on a climb) and its limit, the `u64` base, the diagonal ×141/100, the ×(100 + slope)/100, the climb ×150/100 and the saturating cast — is now one private `price_step(base, limit_pct, climb_cm, from, to, kind, cell_cm)` that `move_cost` and the new `LocomotionCosts::step` both call. `move_cost` keeps its signature and its error order (`NoLocomotion` from `max_slope_pct`, then `Class(to.class)` from `cost`, then the slope). Its other callers (the window walk, `mush-tactics::ground_move_cost`, the arena's slope tests) are untouched and green.
2. **The dense row** (`physics.rs`, re-exported from `crates/mush-atlas/src/lib.rs`). `CLASS_COUNT = TerrainClass::ALL.len()` (18) and `LocomotionCosts { costs: [Option<Cost>; 18] by TerrainClass::code(), max_slope_pct, climb_cm }` (`Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq`): `resolve(table, locomotion, tags)` fills each slot from `table.cost(class.label(), ..)` (the tag merge reused, never re-derived), the limit from `table.max_slope_pct` (its `None` is `Err(NoLocomotion)`), the climb from `table.climb_cm`; `impassable()` (every slot `None`, limit 0, climb 0); `cost(class)`; `cheapest_on(&Cells)` (one pass marking the present codes, then the least passable flat cost, `None` when nothing is passable); `step(from, to, kind, cell_cm)` = `cost(to.class).ok_or(Class)` then `price_step`. Every slot read goes through `.get`, so the crate's deny-lints stay at zero. There was nothing to intern: a `Cell` carries the `#[repr(u8)]` enum, not a string (R1), and the table has one slope limit and one climb per locomotion (R2).
3. **The slice accessor** (`crates/mush-atlas/src/cells.rs`). `Cells::as_slice(&self) -> &[Cell]` (`#[must_use]`), row-major from the south-west, read by `cheapest_on`; the search's inner loop still reads through `Cells::get` (lever L1 was not needed).
4. **The search** (`physics.rs` `path`, signature unchanged). It resolves its row once per call (an unknown locomotion resolves to `impassable()`, so it answers exactly what the string-keyed search did: A5) and steers by `octile_floor(orth, (x, y), to)` = `diag × min(dx, dy) + orth × (max − min)` with `orth` the cheapest passable class present on the surface and `diag = ⌊orth × 141 / 100⌋`, in place of `Chebyshev × 100`. The heap key `Reverse((f, g, y, x))` and the strict `ng < best` are as they were (R7; L3 not applied). The doc carries the admissibility and consistency argument and the arena's `min_move_cost` precedent; the module header gains "plus one pass over the grid per search" and the cut AP paragraph, scoped by the fix round: every row whose passable classes all cost ≥ 100 (every shipped row but `wheeled`; the drive's `tracked`) returns the cost the old search returned, and a row with a class under 100 was over-estimated before and now gets the least. On Ahuna Flank the corner search visits 20,635 cells, down from 58,159.
5. **The home field over the same row** (`crates/tacsim/src/surface/drive.rs`). `HomeField::build` resolves `LocomotionCosts::resolve(table, "tracked", &[])` once a build (`impassable()` on `Err`, which is what `move_cost` answered step by step) and relaxes through a private `dense_step(surface, &costs, from, to)` mirroring `step_cost`; the order, the heap key, the strict improvement and `next` are the base commit's. `drive_leg`, `points_of`, `step_cost` and `home_bound_cost_per_cell` are untouched, so every leg is still re-priced by the string rule (R11). The module header and `HomeField`'s doc say so; `LocomotionCosts` joins the import list.
6. **The measurement is a gate** (`crates/tacsim/tests/driving.rs` `sm4b_the_drive_planner_is_measured`, name kept). Five samples each, min and median printed; in a release build, always, on the minimum: planning corner to corner ≤ 10 ms, the home field over the cached composite ≤ 20 ms, the exhausted flood ≤ 20 ms; in debug under `TACSIM_ASSERT=1` (read as `tests/harness.rs` reads it) the lead's 100 / 250 / 250 ms; in plain debug (the CI shard) SM.4b's `< plan_stop × 10` / `< home_stop × 10` on the median, byte for byte; the keyless capture and build keep `< home_stop × 10` in every build; and outside the timed loop the corner leg from pose (500, 500) on the keyed cached composite must cost `AP_AHUNA_CORNER_COST` 60,720 (294 cells, 18 waypoints), its `visited` printed. `median_ms` takes `&[f64]`; `min_ms` is new. Release on this box: planning 3.28 ms (median 3.46; was 28.86 / 29.57), home field 7.04 (7.65; was 31.32 / 33.06), exhausted 8.31 (8.98; was 28.99 / 30.70), keyless 8.33 (8.82; was 30.46 / 32.82); debug 22.21 / 84.63 / 65.47 / 103.62 ms minimums (were 151.97 / 193.59 / 156.14 / 215.37). No Step 4 lever was needed.
7. **The proofs** (tests). `physics.rs`: A1 `ap_the_dense_row_prices_every_step_as_move_cost_does` (nine base locomotions + unknown `spider` + extension `spider2` × five tag sets × 18 × 18 class pairs × ten rises × both step kinds × 1 m and 10 m cells = 712,800 cases, asserted, `Err` variants included); A2 `ap_the_search_finds_the_least_cost_a_plain_dijkstra_finds` (64 × 64 hash grids of fourteen classes with ±150 cm relief at 100 and 1,000 cm, six locomotions × `[]`/`["amphibious"]` × 16 pairs: `Found` ⇔ the reference's least with the cells re-summed by `move_cost`, `Unreachable` ⇔ `None`; 193 found, 191 unreachable); A3 `ap_the_heuristic_never_overestimates_and_is_consistent` (`h(goal) = 0`, `h(n) ≤ step + h(n′)` on every cell and passable neighbour, `h ≤` the least cost to the goal on 32 samples from a reverse flood cross-checked against `reference_least`); A4 `ap_a_straight_diagonal_over_one_footing_visits_about_its_own_cells` (256² regolith at 10 m, tracked: 256 cells, cost 53,805, visited 256 ≤ 512); A5 `ap_an_unknown_locomotion_answers_as_before` (`Found{cost 0, visited 1}`, `Unreachable{visited 1}`, `OverBudget{1}`, with the derivation from the old body). `drive.rs`: A6 `ap_the_home_field_is_byte_identical_to_the_string_rule` (the whole struct against SM.4b's body verbatim on flat regolith, `noisy()`, the ring-walled `noisy()` and the serpentine); A7 `ap_a_leg_costs_the_least_a_plain_dijkstra_finds` (sixteen `drive_leg` costs on `noisy()` from (30, 40) against a forward Dijkstra over `step_cost`). `tests/driving.rs`: B1 `ap_every_lane_leg_costs_the_least_and_what_it_did` with the reusable `least_from_cell` oracle over `move_cost` on each lane site's keyless terrain from the ramp — all 64 field middles accepted on every site, each leg's cost the flood's least, and the six site totals equal to `AP_SITE_LEG_COST_TOTALS` recorded on the old search (ahuna 1,094,385; commons 1,039,283; juling 1,072,064; kerwan 1,086,989; occator 1,063,028; rheasilvia 1,056,596), the entry order asserted; the tolerance histogram (64/0/0/0 everywhere) and the waypoint and path-cell spreads printed.
8. **Nothing else moved**: no lane, pack, digest, `LOCOMOTION_DIGEST`, budget constant, fixture (`sm4b_the_site_map_fixtures_are_blessed` passes unblessed), CI file, help, web, `docs/design/` or SM.7 file; no file under `crates/mush-pixel`, `deploy/` or the TUI pixel view.

### Deferred, and why

- **The debug pair (100 / 250 / 250 ms) is asserted only under `TACSIM_ASSERT=1`** (the brief's R8; an owner-critical default standing until the owner rules). The lead's note names the figures; asserting them in the push-triggered debug CI shard (`-j 2`, beside the other heavy integration binaries) would gate CI on a shared runner's speed, which D-H-8 forbids and D-16-19 says only an owner wish supersedes. The default: the release gate binds every `--release` run (no CI job runs `tests/driving.rs` in release — R9: the weekly `scale` and `tacsim-harness` jobs run `--release` only on their own `#[ignore]` harnesses, and the `release` job only builds binaries); the gate runner's `TACSIM_ASSERT=1` debug line asserts the lead's pair; CI keeps SM.4b's ceilings. The margins the owner can see: debug minimums 22.2 ms planning against 100, 84.6 ms home field against 250, 65.5 ms exhausted against 250 (the gate run read 23.0 / 87.1 / 62.3). If the owner wants CI to gate, the change is to drop the environment check and record it under D-16-19.
- **Item 5, the RAM memo of the last planned leg (so `go` after a preview does not search again): not built** (the brief's R10; the lead's "if it complicates the order slot, leave it and say so"). SM.7 generalised `DriveOrders` into the one-slot-per-rig `ActOrders`, whose invariant is "the newer order replaces the older"; a memo keyed by site revision would be a third kind of entry in that slot. With the gate met, a preview plus `go` costs two searches of about 3.3 ms each. SM.12's cost lane may reopen it if its measurements ask.
- **Lever L1 (slice reads in the inner loops), L2 (one per-cell record) and L3 (the deeper-first tie order) were not applied**: the first release measurement after Steps 1–3 already met the gate (3.50 / 6.60 / 9.11 ms), so the brief said stop. `as_slice` therefore serves only `cheapest_on`; its doc was corrected by the fix round to say so.
- **R5, the floor is the cheapest class present on the surface, not the row's cheapest** (lead/planner ruling): the tracked row's cheapest is paved/road at 100, the lane's sites hold only regolith 150, ice 200 and rock 300, and a step can only enter a cell on the surface — the arena's `min_move_cost` precedent. A4 pins that the present-class floor is in force (orth 100 would visit far more than 512 cells).
- **R6, `wheeled` (paved 90, road 80) and any extension row priced under 100 may now return a cheaper path than before and may visit more cells** (lead ruling; the one carve-out from "a pin whose cost changes is a bug"): the old `Chebyshev × 100` over-estimated there. No production caller searches wheeled (the drive is tracked), no pin covers a wheeled cost, and `physics.rs`'s wheeled test pins only `Found(_)`. The doc comments say so after the fix round; A2 proves the least cost against the reference Dijkstra.
- **R7, the tie order kept; one tie moved on Ahuna Flank** (allowed by the brief's freeze rule): the 64 ramp legs' waypoint spread went 3/12/24 → 3/13/24, every cost equal (B1), 64/64 accepted at tolerance 1, the maximum still 24 (doc 20 §13's SM.4b "at most 24 waypoints" stands). Not in the builder's TESTS CHANGED section (reviewers N3/T4) — carried here. A re-planned Ahuna drive may show different waypoints, length and arrival heading at the same cost and time.
- **The arena's own A* (`tacsim::arena::path`) is not a caller and was not touched** (R12); `mush-sim`, `tacsim --test arena` and `mush-tactics` ran as regression only.
- **R3's shared `price_step` reads `climb_cm` eagerly** in `move_cost` (it is pure) — a deviation in evaluation order with no observable difference.
- **A3's oracle**: 30 of its 32 samples are bounded by a reverse flood over `move_cost(next, here)`, cross-checked against `reference_least` on two; the brief named `reference_least` for all 32. Equivalent, recorded as a deviation.
- **The doc gate ran as `--exclude mush-pixel`** (the lead's 0a note) and `cargo fmt --check` was judged on the cut's five files alone; the brief's combined `--test restriction_lints --test panic_budget` line was re-run split once by the builder when the owner's then-unfixed `mush-net-ssh` budget stopped it (green at the gate after 966a1c08).
- **Not in this cut**: SM.12's off-loop keyed site-ground runner and the 64-TV cohort; any change to `locomotion.json`, `LOCOMOTION_DIGEST`, the terrain classes, `DEFAULT_PATH_MAX_CELLS`, `DRIVE_PATH_BUDGET_CELLS`, the freeze, `MAX_LEG_WAYPOINTS`, `path_max_cells`; a CI release job; the doc 20 amendment and this note (the lead's).

### Residual risks the judge named

- The admissibility argument fails only at the Cost::MAX saturation edge: `price_step` saturates a step at u32::MAX while `octile_floor`'s `diag = orth × 141 / 100` is uncapped in u64, so an extension row whose cheapest present class costs more than about 3.05e9 makes the diagonal floor overestimate and `path` could return a non-least path there. No shipped row comes within six orders of magnitude; a one-line `.min(u64::from(Cost::MAX))` on `diag` closes it when the next cut touches physics.rs.
- The release branch and the TACSIM_ASSERT=1 debug branch assert only the minimum of five (10/20/20 and 100/250/250 ms); SM.4b's median ceilings (< 200/200/500 ms release, < 2,500/2,500/20,000 ms debug) are kept only in the plain-debug CI branch and on the keyless build. A regression that slows four of five samples while one stays fast would pass the release gate. The brief ordered this shape; keeping the old median asserts beside the new minimum ones costs nothing and cannot flake.
- One equal-cost tie broke the other way on Ahuna Flank (waypoint spread 3/12/24 → 3/13/24 over the 64 ramp legs; every cost equal per B1, all 64 accepted at tolerance 1, maximum still 24). A leg's frozen waypoints, `metres` and arrival `heading_mdeg` derive from the exact cells, so a player re-planning that Ahuna drive after deploy may see a different waypoint count, length or arrival heading at the same cost and time. R7 allows it and nothing stored compares against it, but the builder's "no player-facing change" is overstated by that much.
- A2 asserts its coverage only in aggregate (`found > 0 && unreachable > 0`; it printed 193/191), so a fixture or table drift that made a whole (cell size × locomotion) slice trivially unreachable would still pass; and A3 checks consistency per edge only on untagged rows (A2 covers `["amphibious"]` end to end only). Pinning the exact 193/191 and looping A3 over the same two tag sets would close both cheaply.
- The release exhausted-flood figure is the tightest margin: min 9.69 ms (median 10.36) against the 20 ms gate at the final gate run, measured with B1 running in the same binary in parallel; the builder's quiet run read 8.31 ms. A heavily loaded gate box could cross 20 ms on the minimum of five. The gate runner's line, not CI, carries this.
- The measured test's doc sentence "ten times the old STOP, 250 ms planning and 2,000 ms a build" reads as if the debug CI ceilings were 250/2,000 ms; the asserted ceilings are those × 10 (2,500 and 20,000 ms).
- `visited` counts and `OverBudget` answers of `path` change for every caller (Ahuna's corner search visits 20,635 cells, down from 58,159); the only production caller (`drive_leg`, tracked, budget = the whole grid) cannot turn a `Found` into `OverBudget`, and for a row with a class under 100 (wheeled, no production caller) a tight budget could now answer `OverBudget` where the old over-estimating search found a path. The doc says so; no pin covered it.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and the verbatim strict `cargo doc` stay red on the owner's unpushed pixel files only (CRLF and a public doc linking a private item); the lead lands by cherry-pick onto origin/main where those commits are absent, so the cut's own tree is clean, but the local checkout's gate remains two-red until the owner's commits are fixed or pushed.

**Lead rulings taken (the brief's §0, all eight):** (1) the recover stays one act; the unload is a second act on the one start/finish, queued durably by the recover's `Done` and submitted by the tick as the operator — built as `RigRecord.queued`, R1. (2) `+tv/unload [qty]`: a bare preview of `min(hopper, room)` per good, `go` commits exactly that, `[qty]` one good at a time (the first in id order, R10), `UNLOAD_S` 600 a code constant (R13), the unload spends nothing and recharges in the bay. (3) one hold-room function (`hold_unreserved_with`, the unloading rig left out); a hopper the hold cannot take unloads what fits and says what stays, never refuses the recover. (4) the plan generalised (`stowage_plan`/`plan_check`), `governed_hold` and `PortCapacity::plan` untouched; the hopper refused at sale by `HOLD_ONLY_SOURCE` and `may_take`, pinned. (5) the story in `mush-server/tests/sm_story.rs`, twin arms over one fixed key (R11, R17). (6) `mining.md` complete and the help gates green. (7) no RNG, no truth leak, LANE_VERSION 11, no new verb beyond the `+tv` switch. (8) the gates re-blessed as listed under pins.

**Owner-critical defaults, standing until the owner rules:** R5 — an unload works only on a site's pad (`UNLOAD_NOT_SITE`), and so at a port the departure reads `HOPPER_LOADED_AWAY` ("staff must empty it"); if the owner allows unloading at a dock, the gate and the port line go away in one change. R6 — the queued unload is not gated on the operator being aboard (the recover's `go` committed it aboard); the hand unload is. R7 — a queued unload the hold cannot take at all is a 0 s act told once (`UNLOADED_NONE`), never a stuck queue. R8 — the finish refuses `HoldRefused` rather than overfill (staff state only). The new player-facing texts for review: `RECOVER_THEN`, `RECOVER_THEN_PART`, `RECOVER_THEN_NONE`, `UNLOAD_PREVIEW`, `UNLOAD_STAYS`, `UNLOAD_FILED`, `UNLOADED`, `UNLOADED_NONE`, `RECOVERED_UNLOADING`, `UNLOAD_UNDER_WAY`, `UNLOAD_NOT_SITE`, `UNLOAD_OUT`, `UNLOAD_NO_ROOM`, `UNLOAD_NO_FIT`, `UNLOAD_CHANGED`, `UNLOAD_USAGE`, `WHY_LEFT_BAY`, `WHY_HOLD_REFUSED`, `WHY_MARKERS_FULL` (the fix round's), `QUEUED_LINE`, the reworded `HOPPER_LOADED`, `HOPPER_LOADED_AWAY`, the `+tv` help and recover help lines, and the offer's presentation text ("…bring it in, unload its hopper into the hold, or empty it onto the spoil.").

**Declared deviations from the brief:** a stale queued start (the queue gone, no order) is refused `ProviderRejected` "that act was not planned" at the offer, not `Conflict` — the race loser does get `Conflict` (U9 pins both); `{ore}` in `UNLOAD_NO_FIT` is SM.7's `ore_words` ("ice ore"), not the commodity label; `FixedPlan.params` is `None` for an unload, the facts in `FixedPlan.unload`; U4 proves `RIG_BUSY` with an unload in flight (a recover in flight reads `UNLOAD_OUT` first by the gate order); `unload_room` requires exactly one ore compartment; `hold_unreserved_with` maps a non-accepted hopper good or an overflowing product to `None`; the story sets a shared real start (`story_t0`), bunkers +2 t and +3 crew-days over the planner's figures (the leg home with 12 t aboard and the pad days), runs 8 warm fires after the restart point in both arms, and tells `RECOVERED_UNLOADING` and submits the queued start on one fire.

**Deferred to later cuts, and why:** the ≤ 8 writes a completion of §11's Tick row — the unload finish measured and pinned at 9–19 (fresh pool 10, two goods 17, existing pool 9, 8 evictions 17, two goods with 3 evictions 19); the brief forbade trimming the inventory's writes to meet it, so SM.12's cost lane gates on it. The marker-ring bound (128 young markers a hopper vault per real day, about 64 two-ore unloads, carried across lessees) — a residual the owner should see beside the texts; a staff tool to clear a ring, or a per-lease ring, is SM.12's if wanted. A queued unload whose operator lost the helm or charter retries and pages until any start lands — SM.11/SM.12 (a plan's chain reuses `Queued`). The store-table-versus-plan refusal in `unload_room` is untestable without a seam the brief forbade building. The `UNLOADED_NONE` line on an empty queued hopper, the `UNLOAD_NO_FIT` wording when the hopper's stock binds, and the comma-joined multi-good lines are text items for the owner's review, not built. The quarry screen, claims, plans and `await tv`, the mill and any staff verb that empties a hopper at a port are SM.9–SM.12 by the brief's §5.

- crates/tacsim/tests/mining.rs `recovered()`: in its new unload branch the direct `last == (Recover, Done)` assertion is replaced by `last == (Unload, Done)` after finishing the unload; the recover's Done is implied (only a Done recover writes the queue and only a queue starts a queued unload) but no longer asserted directly, and `emptied()` after it is now a no-op. One line restores it; not weakened in substance.
- crates/mush-server/tests/sm_story.rs: the story's doc comment at line 1490 says "A3" (it is A1; A3 is the two-rig test), `play` prints the mined pockets (`println!`, against the brief's "print nothing"), and the bunker margins (+2 t, +3 crew-days over the planner's figures, line 1171) are explained only by a code comment — the planner's own figures are therefore not shown to suffice for a mining trip with 12 t aboard.
- §11's Tick row (≤ 8 writes a completion) is not met by the unload finish: measured and pinned at 10 (one good, fresh hold pool), 17 (two goods, one fresh pool), 9 (one good, existing pool), 17 (one good with 8 ring evictions) and 19 (two goods with 3 evictions). Nothing was trimmed, as the brief ordered; SM.12's cost lane gates on it.
- The hopper's marker ring is the hopper vault's (Occator's rig) and outlives a lease: MAX_MARKER_RING 128 young markers per 86,400 real s, about 64 two-ore unloads a real day before `MarkersFull` refuses; the refusal is now its own code and text, but the bound carries across lessees.
- `UNLOADED_NONE` fills `{stays}` from an empty map when a queued unload's hopper read empty at the offer (staff emptied it after the recover): a broken line on a staff-only path (correctness/F4, not fixed).
- `UNLOAD_NO_FIT` says "{q} t do not fit" when the binding term is the hopper's stock rather than the hold's room (unload.rs `part`: fit = min(available, units_in)); a player with 4 t of ice and an empty hold hears "5 t do not fit" (correctness/F6).
- A queued unload whose operator no longer holds the helm or the charter (staff-ended charter, helm change) is refused Unauthorized at every attempt: 8 tries, one page a boot, then a retry every 60 fires, until any start lands on the rig (correctness/F7; repossession and the lease return refuse a loaded hopper, so only staff make it).

- `RECOVERED_UNLOADING` may be told on the same fire an operator's own act (a dump `go` typed before the fire) supersedes the queue: the tell reads the record before the superseding start lands.
- `unload_room`'s refusal when the store's goods table differs from the plan's (`None`, logged) has no test: no seam sets the store's table apart from the compiled one; `sm8_the_unload_weighs_with_the_plans_table` pins table equality and the digest fail-closed only, and its doc comment now says so.

The lead's rulings on the judge's residuals and the round's review:

- **The hopper vault's marker ring, for the owner and for SM.11.** `MAX_MARKER_RING` keeps 128 young markers a vault per 86,400 real seconds, about 64 two-ore unloads a real day, and the ring is the hopper's, so it carries across lessees. At rate 24 a real day is 24 IC days and a 288-IC-hour plan is 12 real hours: a plan unloading more often than every four to five IC hours can fill the ring and have its unload refused `markers_full` until the oldest marker ages out. SM.11's interpreter must treat `MarkersFull` as a wait with the record's back-off (never a park) and name it in the reconnect summary, and its builder measures the ring's headroom at the story's cadence; if the cap binds, the lead's ruling is to make the vault's ring window the act's retry horizon rather than a real day (the idempotency key already guards the action's own replay), recorded here for the owner.
- **§11's Tick row (≤ 8 writes a completion), deferred to SM.12.** The unload finish is pinned at 10, 17, 9, 17 and 19 writes (one good into a fresh pool; two goods; an existing pool; eight ring evictions; two goods with three evictions); the brief forbade trimming the inventory's writes to meet the row, so SM.12's cost lane gates on it with the measurement in hand.
- **A queued unload whose operator lost the helm or the charter, residual (SM.11/SM.12).** It is refused Unauthorized at every attempt — eight tries, one page a boot, then a retry every 60 fires — until any start lands on the rig; only staff reach it (the repossession and the lease return refuse a loaded hopper). SM.11's plan chain reuses `Queued`, so its interpreter drops an orphaned queue with a page.
- **`RECOVERED_UNLOADING` on the superseding fire, residual.** The tell reads the record before an operator's own dump `go` typed before the fire lands and supersedes the queue; one misleading line, nothing moves wrongly.
- **The store-table-versus-plan refusal in `unload_room`, residual.** `None` and a log when the store's goods table differs from the plan's; no seam sets them apart, so `sm8_the_unload_weighs_with_the_plans_table` pins table equality and the digest fail-closed only, and says so.
- **The story's bunkers, a doc 18 residual for the owner.** The story bunkers more than doc 18's planner says (the margins are the measured constants `STORY_EXTRA_BURN_T` 0 and `STORY_EXTRA_CREW_DAYS` 1, asserted exactly against the planner's own lines): the planner prices the passage as laden at departure, and the leg home with 12 t of ore aboard and the pad days are outside its figures. A mining captain who bunkers to the planner's line is a crew-day short for the way home (the laden leg home from Ahuna's pad is priced at 2 crew-days against the planner's 1; the burn gap is 0); the planner should take an expected cargo mass — doc 18's, not this train's.

Verdict: ship after R1 and R2, which are one-line changes; take the notes at the lead's discretion.

- **R1** (should-fix): mining.rs:2439-2447: `let filed = record.queued.is_some();` then `if !filed { assert_eq!(started, None, "an empty hopper files nothing"); return; }`. The helper picks its branch from what the system under test wrote, the record's queue, and never reads the hopper to decide. None of its three callers reaches the `!filed` branch: in sm7_rights_gate_mining_and_never_the_way_home, parts (b), (c) and (e) recover with 4, 2 and 2 t aboard. So suppose a loaded recover stops filing its unload (a regression of lead ruling 1). The helper then asserts only that nothing started and returns green, and its message "an empty hopper files nothing" is never checked. Today a later CYCLE_DONE `{hopper}` pin catches that after (b) and (c), with a confusing message; nothing catches it after (e). This is not a weakening against the judge tree, whose `else` arm had the same hole, but the helper's new doc says it unloads "with ore in the hopper", and the code does not check that.
- **R2** (should-fix): mining.md:157-159 now reads "a number past what the hopper holds of it, or past what the hold has room for, is refused, and the refusal names the number that does." The old sentence ("past what fits … names the number that does") had "fits" as the verb that "does" stood for. The rewrite removed "fits", so in this player-facing help "does" no longer refers to anything.
- **N1** (note): sm_story.rs:80 `const STORY_EXTRA_BURN_T: u64 = 0;` and :88 `const STORY_EXTRA_CREW_DAYS: u64 = 1;`, with the measure at :1345-1369. This is the fixer's flagged deviation: it set the measured gaps and asserts them exactly, rather than lifting the build's +2/+3 as named constants. I checked the measure and it is not circular. `burn_need = tank_at_lift - tank_on_pad + laden_burn` and `days_need = locker_at_lift - locker_on_pad + laden_days` come from the pre-lift `+ship/plan ahuna` (read at :1220-1223) and the on-pad `+ship/plan ceres`. Both are whole pool units from voyage.rs:1991/2001 (`basis.tank`, `basis.locker`), so they are independent of how much was bunkered. The planner is unchanged: voyage.rs is not in the delta. `days_need > bare_days` proves the crew-day margin is needed, as item 2(c) asked. Exact equality is stronger than `<=`. Two side effects: the story now lands at Ceres with no reserve, and `saturating_sub` reads a planner that over-prices as a 0 gap, which is acceptable because no margin is then needed. The `>` assertion is implied by the equality with 1, but it gives a clearer message.
- **N2** (note): sm_story.rs:18-19 (module doc): "bunkers to the planner's figures for Ahuna Flank (the leg home held back)". The step-3 comment at :1179 says the same: "bunker to the planner's own figures for Ahuna, the leg home held back." The story now bunkers `STORY_EXTRA_CREW_DAYS` past those figures. Item 2(c) asked for that gap to stand visibly, but the two summaries a reader sees first do not mention it.
- **N3** (note): tv.rs:618 is a placeholder-block comment line about 140 columns wide: "// commas, so a plain ", " join was ambiguous — the lead's pre-commit round, item 5), `{room}` the hold's unreserved mass after the unload in". rustfmt does not wrap comments, so `--check` passes; the rest of the block keeps to 100 columns.
- **N4** (note): act.rs:2181 `fn and_list` is the third private copy of the `a`, `a and b`, `a, b and c` join, after match_/cockpit.rs:8639 `join_names` and the inline one at match_/report.rs:707. unloading.rs:1199-1203's `words` helper re-implements it too, though U3 pins the two-good literal independently, which is fine. The lead allowed a private function, since no shared helper exists. load_words also feeds the dump's preview and filed lines (act.rs:2549), so a multi-good dump now reads as a list too. That is consistent, but the fixer's return does not say so. A repo-wide grep shows no pinned multi-good dump, unload, help or design text that used the old ", " join.

The start `tacsim_surface_act` takes optional `how` (Choice part|queued|whole) and `qty` (Integer 1..=99): an unload must carry `how`, and `qty` exactly with `part`; any other act carrying either is `InvalidRequest` "an unload names how it was planned"; a `queued` start needs the offer's queued variant for its ordinal AND the record's queue; a hand start needs the hand variant with equal `how`/`qty`; else `Conflict` "that rig's orders moved on"; the re-check refuses `ProviderRejected unload_changed`.
**tacsim::surface::tick**: `pub(crate) const QUEUED_CYCLE: u8 = u8::MAX` (attempts key `(tv, record.ordinal + 1, QUEUED_CYCLE)`, never in `finish_retried`); the queued candidate on an idle record; `submit_queued` (private) submits `{ tv, act: "unload", ordinal, how: "queued" }` under `queued_key` through `Fire::as_principal`; `completion_line(ctx, record, last, hull)`.
**tacsim::port::tv** (pub): `RECOVER_THEN`, `RECOVER_THEN_PART`, `RECOVER_THEN_NONE`, `UNLOAD_PREVIEW`, `UNLOAD_STAYS`, `UNLOAD_FILED`, `UNLOADED`, `UNLOADED_NONE`, `RECOVERED_UNLOADING`, `UNLOAD_UNDER_WAY`, `UNLOAD_NOT_SITE`, `UNLOAD_OUT`, `UNLOAD_NO_ROOM`, `UNLOAD_NO_FIT`, `UNLOAD_CHANGED`, `UNLOAD_USAGE`, `WHY_LEFT_BAY`, `WHY_HOLD_REFUSED`, `WHY_MARKERS_FULL`, `QUEUED_LINE`, `MAX_TYPED_TONNES: u64 = 99`; the four `RECOVER_*PREVIEW` templates carry `{then}` after `hopper {hopper}`; `Act::Unload { qty: Option<u64>, go: bool }`, `ACT_WORDS` 14, `TV_USAGE`/`TV_HELP` with `+tv[/<n>]/unload [<t>] [go]`; `rig_state` prints `QUEUED_LINE`.
**tacsim::port::voyage** (pub): `HOPPER_LOADED` (reworded: "+tv/{n} unload moves it into the hold, or +tv/{n} dump empties it onto the spoil."), `HOPPER_LOADED_AWAY` ("staff must empty it."); `bay_gate` picks by `pad`.
**commands.rs**: the `+tv` switch list gains "unload".

### Doc 20 amendments owed

§1 beat 9 — the example "home in 25 s; then 12 t metal ore into the hold, 62 t of room" and the SM.4b note: as built (SM.8) the preview's clause is `RECOVER_THEN` "; then it unloads 12 t of metal ore, run-of-mine into the hold, 74 t of room after" (a Dray-P's 86 t hold with nothing else aboard; the label is goods v3's), or `RECOVER_THEN_PART`/`RECOVER_THEN_NONE` when the room is short; the recover lands and tells `RECOVERED_UNLOADING`, the queued unload starts on the next fire and tells `UNLOADED` 600 IC s later; `+tv/1 unload [<t>]` does it by hand.
§4.1 and §11's Charge row — "bay recharge … unloads included": as built, `UNLOAD_S` 600 is a code constant and U11 pins the regain at 600 × 50,000 / 3,600 = 8,333 cu, capped at the capacity; the unload reserves nothing and reads no battery.
§4.3 — `HOPPER_LOADED`'s sentence: as built it names `+tv/{n} unload` first and the dump beside it on a site's pad, and `HOPPER_LOADED_AWAY` ("staff must empty it") anywhere else, both under `DepartRefusalKind::HopperLoaded`; a queued unload is not busy to the gate (the lead's R5, an owner-critical default standing until the owner rules).
§6 — "`+tv/recover` always unloads everything": as built it holds by construction for an honest fill; a staff-shrunk hold unloads what fits and says what stays (`UNLOAD_STAYS`), and a hold with no room at all makes the queued unload a 0 s act told once as `UNLOADED_NONE` (R7); the row's "the hold's unreserved room is read by mining and the map only … SM.8 must answer" is answered so: the unload's own room is `hold_unreserved_with` with the unloading rig left out, re-checked at its start, and the finish admits against the hold's limit less its load — no other hold writer was changed.
§7.1 — "`transfer_marked` from the hopper pools to the hold pool … the marker derived from `(tv, excursion, ordinal)`": as built the finish is ONE inventory-owned `transfer_many_marked` (one `inventory.transferred` marker a good, the id from `(tv, excursion|null, ordinal, good)` at the act's due; the hopper vault's marker ring written once), because two `transfer_marked` calls cannot share a bundle; "its own act" is `act = unload` on SM.3b's one start and finish, no third action; the recover's `Done` writes a durable `RigRecord.queued` in its own bundle and the surface tick starts it as the operator under `tacsim.surface/{tv}/{ordinal}/queued` with `how: queued`; `+tv/unload [qty]` sends `how: whole` or `how: part, qty`, the start bound to its RAM order (`ActOrder::Unload`) by them and the queued start to the record's queue, each re-checked at the prepare (`unload_changed`); a part unload takes the first good in id order (R10) and `UNLOAD_NO_FIT` names the fit, never clamped; "`plan_of(&LogisticsDef)` … generalised" is `stowage_plan`/`plan_compartments`/`plan_goods`/`plan_check`, `PortCapacity::check` now deserialise + `plan_check`, `PortCapacity::plan` and `governed_hold` unchanged (R12); the unload works only on a site's pad (R5) and the queued unload reads no "aboard" (R6) — both owner-critical defaults standing until the owner rules.
§7.2 and §7.4 — pinned as written: the hopper refused at sale by `may_take` (`NO_SUCH_LISTING`) and `HOLD_ONLY_SOURCE` (U12), and the story's sale pays the Trust `margin_and_share(price, reference_minor, 12, 250)` (87.50 cr on 12 t at 70.00 cr against 35.00 cr); add "As built (SM.8): the story on `build_engine` at rate 24 sells the unloaded hold with no staff act at all" to §13's "one staff act (the rate)".
§8 — the acts list "recover done, unload done": as built the tick has a fourth candidate reason, a queued unload on an idle record, submitted under its own attempts key `(tv, ordinal, QUEUED_CYCLE)` that is never a finish's retry; "nothing is RAM-only" holds for the queue (U7 and the story's restart: the post-image after a `build_engine` restart equals the straight run's), while a hand `+tv/unload go`'s order is RAM like a drive's ("that act was not planned; preview it again" after a restart); the finish's offer now also fixes the real second `wall` (the market lot offer's precedent) for the marker ring, so the finish's fixed parameters are not a pure function of IC time.
§11 Tick row — "≤ 8 writes a completion … unmeasured until SM.12": as built (SM.8) the unload finish is measured and pinned at 10 (one good into a fresh hold pool), 17 (two goods, one fresh pool), 9 (one good into an existing pool), 17 (with 8 marker-ring evictions) and 19 (two goods with 3 evictions) — over the row, nothing trimmed, SM.12's cost lane gates on it.
§13 SM.8 row — add "As built: landed as above; the acceptance's A1–A5 and U1–U12, U9b, A3 pinned by `tests/unloading.rs` (18), `mush-inventory/tests/sm8.rs` (5) and `mush-server/tests/sm_story.rs`; the story needed no staff act; doc 20 is Draft 0.9 as built through SM.8" and move the README row's draft and landed-hash list.
§14 D-20-10 — add "As built (SM.8): the capacity plan over any stowage block (`stowage_plan`/`plan_check`), the hopper refused at sale twice and never planned by the market"; D-20-11 — add "As built (SM.8): the unload as `act = unload` on the one start and finish, queued durably on the record by a `Done` recover and started by the tick as the operator; the start's `how`/`qty` bind it to its source as `to` binds a drive"; D-20-7 — the departure's two hopper lines.
§16 — add the marker-ring bound as a risk: a hopper vault's ring holds 128 markers younger than 86,400 real s (about 64 two-ore unloads a real day) before `MarkersFull` refuses an unload until they age, and the ring is the vault's, so it carries across lessees; and the queued unload whose operator lost the helm or charter retrying until any start lands.

## SM.9

**The quarry screen and the ground chart** (doc 20 §13's SM.9 row; §3.1, §10 — D-20-13): the
pulled `body.ground` grid feed and `+chart/ground [<body>]` (lists) / `+chart/ground map [<body>]
[<family>]` (draws: the wash `.`/`-`/`+`/`*` of one family, the ports by their label's initial, the
sites by letter, the passage planned at the viewer's hull's load through one `vantage_reading`,
", where you are." for the site the hull stands at, the best reading from the keyed site context so
it prints after any restart); the TUI lettered screen `q` (the twelfth screen, third gated: `z`
steps drive → site → ground, `t` picks the next rig, the digits global) and the web quarry
`FeedScreen` on `site.map`, both placing the viewer's own rigs along the frame's `rigs[].leg` from
`site.clock` and `site.under` by SM.4b's `leg_position` rule (the lead's 0z ruling: clients
interpolate, no timer, re-pull on `tv.status` only); the pushed `tv.status` keyframe carrying the
operator's whole projection (`rig: TvRec`, `RunView` naming the pocket address and the family's
good, never class, yield or tonnes — SM.7's rule reversed by the lead) from `write_projection` only
when the store wrote; the projection's log kept to its current operator's excursion; `site.map`'s
vector keys (legend `v`/`V`/`#`, `addressed`, `families`, `grid`, `marks`, `under`, `clock`, `log`,
the readings' and rigs' lines, `rigs[].queued`, `hold`, and `no_readings` / `other_rigs`,
the side panes' two sentences whole) with no line-mode glyph or line moved; a frame that drops the
picked rig clears the pick on both clients;
`PanelSubscribe.params` (≤ 512 bytes, object only) so the web asks for a view, rig, family or body;
the site and ground fixtures blessed; `docs/help/tui.md`'s lettered screens `c` and `q`. The ground
frame's rows run south-first like every grid frame (the planner's D17 reversed at the judge). No
lane, pack or digest moved. Built 2026-10-21/22 on main from `9922c9c7` (the Draft 0.9 docs commit
`b74a01ed` landing under the run). Judged **ship-with-notes**; the lead accepted the owner-critical
defaults (the rig key `t`, the two-family `V`, the ground chart's glyphs and the shared-cell listing,
`z`'s cycle, client interpolation with the TUI's ~4 s step, the line-mode body map at one column a
cell, and every new player-facing text) and ran a fix round before the commit (the stale pick, the side panes' keys, the address bound's own
refusal "a rig projection's run address is at most 8 bytes", the 120-column badge floor, and
`docs/help/mining.md`'s "Still to come"). One commit, pushed.

### Deferred, and why

- **D17 reversed — the ground frame's rows run south-first** (lead acceptance): the brief's north-first rule rested on `sky.chart` being a north-up raster, which it is not (`mush_ansi/src/panel.rs` and `chart_panel.rs:144,173` both put row 0 at the south edge). A north-first `body.ground` would be the one grid frame every generic consumer draws upside down. `frame_cell` is the identity, each renderer flips consistently, and the test is `sm9_frame_rows_run_from_the_south_edge`. Accepted at the judge; doc 20 §3.1 to say so.
- **The `site.map` additions** (lead acceptance, item by item): every item of 3.3 plus three beyond the brief — `site.under`, `site.clock`, `rigs[].queued` — and three undeclared small extras: `site.grid.cell_cm` (the clients' leg centimetres), `ground.ports[].lat_mdeg/lon_mdeg` and `ground.sites[].dark` and `.best_line`, and `RunView.good` as `Option<CanonicalId>` (absent on a pre-SM.9 record) rather than the brief's bare `CanonicalId`; and two more from the pre-commit round (the judge's correctness/F10) — `site.no_readings: string|null` and `site.other_rigs: string|null`, the side panes' two sentences whole so no client reads `site.lines` by prefix. All vector keys; no glyph or line moved.
- **The 0z ruling: clients interpolate** (lead ruling, reversing the planner's R-d/D8): the TUI and the web place the viewer's own rigs along `rigs[].leg` with `leg_position`'s rule, from `site.clock` and `site.under`; no 4 s timer, no `QUARRY_PULL_S`, no `quarry_asked_at`, no `heal_queries` change; the screens re-pull on `tv.status` only. The TUI moves a rig on its own paints (about every 4 s via the WHO reply); the web repaints once a second while a leg is in flight. `server.rs` (the owner's) untouched.
- **SM.7's `RunView` rule reversed** under lead ruling 4: the view now names the pocket address and the family's good (the operator's own choices), never class, yield or tonnes.
- **The here site's passage** (the fixer's ruling on correctness/F4): the site the hull stands at carries no passage and reads \"…, where you are.\"; the owner still holds the routing question of the passage home from a site's pad (site ports route only to the Freeport, so every other site reads \"no passage from <site>\").
- **Q7's first fire**: the landed tick projects a start at once only for an act with a leg or a run (SM.4b's P8), so a scan's first fire pushes nothing; Q7 pins that and pins the start push on a drive.
- **Owner-critical defaults standing** (the lead's, for the owner): the rig key `t` (D1; the digits are global screen keys); the two-family `V` (D9); the ground chart's glyphs `.`/`-`/`+`/`*`, the marker letters and the shared-cell \"Also at F: …\" listing (D4); `z` cycling drive → site → ground (R-c); client interpolation with the TUI's ~4 s step; the line-mode body map at one column a cell; and every new player-facing text — the `GROUND_*` texts, `GROUND_SITE_LINE_UNPLANNED`, `MAP_RUN_CLAUSE`, `MAP_CORE_CLAUSE`, the legend labels \"pit, worked\" / \"pit, worked out\" / \"claim\", the TUI's \"(no map yet: r asks the server)\", \"z: the ground chart\", \"(no ground chart yet: r asks the server)\", \"(no rigs here)\", the pane headings \"readings, {family}\" and \"log\", and the web's \"The map the server sent did not read.\", \"No map yet: r asks the server.\", \"No ground chart yet: r asks the server.\", the SVG titles \"your hull\" / \"block {letter}\", the toggles \"picture\" / \"flat map\", the headings \"rigs\" / \"sites\" / \"log\".\n- **Landed in the pre-commit round** (formerly deferred or residual): `docs/help/mining.md`'s \"Still to come\" clause \"the ground chart of a whole body\" dropped (help tripwire `--lib help` 3 passed); the stale rig pick after a return (correctness/F7), cleared on both clients; the side panes' prefix coupling (F10), replaced by `site.no_readings` / `site.other_rigs`; the addr-bound refusal text (F11), its own sentence; the badge test at the 120-column floor (N1). See note_landed item 15.\n- **Not built**: the release run of Q8 (debug: least 20.59 ms, median 21.98 ms); a screen assertion in `sm_story.rs`; a dedicated test for the `leg`-only-on-this-site gate (unreachable in the rig).\n- **Residuals for later cuts**: the log pane emptying at the recover's tell (DEVIATIONS 5, a consequence of D16).

### Residual risks the judge named

- The log pane holds the current excursion only and empties when the rig comes home: a recover's tell writes excursion None, so projection_for starts a clean log there (DEVIATIONS 5). Consistent with D16 but owner-visible as a behaviour of the Right pane.
- The TUI moves a rig only on its own paints (about every 4 s via the WHO reply), so the animation steps rather than glides; a smoother repaint needs a frame clock in server.rs, the owner's file.
- Untested: the server-side gate that emits rigs[].leg only for an act on this site (a rig of the docked hull with an act on another site is unreachable in the test rig); driving stays green.
- From a site's pad, +chart/ground reads "no passage from <site>" for every other site and never shows the passage home on the port line, because site ports route only to the Freeport; a routing/text decision for the owner.

### The lead's fix round (before the commit)

Five items fixed in the lead's pre-commit round (run `wf_2cda992a-726`: a fixer, one reviewer over the fix delta only — no must-fix; its one should-fix, the judge's landing text contradicting the tree, re-fixed in the cut note itself — then the gate, fourteen commands green on the first run): the stale rig pick is cleared on both clients when a held `site.map` frame no longer lists the picked slot (`TuiApp::forget_an_unlisted_quarry_rig` after every keyframe, sharing `quarry_slots` with `t`; `QuarryStore.applySite`), tested through what the next ask carries on the TUI, through the real `GameApp`'s asks on the web, and on the store; `TvRec::check` refuses an over-long run address with its own sentence ("a rig projection's run address is at most 8 bytes"), the cycle bound's text now pinned byte for byte beside it; the tab-badge strip is pinned exactly at the 120-column floor beside the 140-column case; `docs/help/mining.md`'s "Still to come" line loses the ground-chart clause (no pin quoted it); and the side panes read `site.no_readings` and `site.other_rigs` (two additive `string | null` keys carrying the whole unwrapped sentences) instead of picking `site.lines` by prefix — `lines`, `print` and line mode byte-identical, the two site fixtures re-blessed for the keys only, a wrapped other-rigs sentence rendered whole on both clients (`QuarryScreen.test.ts` new), `driving.rs`'s `without_mark` helper also normalising the new key. The round's review notes: the cleared pick does not re-ask by itself, so a `MAP_NO_RIG` reason frame from a stale ask stays on screen until the next `tv.status` push or `r` — handed to SM.10 as an inherited item (a one-shot re-ask when a pick clears on a reason frame while the quarry screen is active, on both clients); clearing on any frame that lists no rigs also drops the pick on a cold or dark reason frame — accepted (a structured reason key on reason frames is a later cut's); three comment-only staleness notes fixed by the lead at landing.

The lead's rulings on the judge's residuals and the round's review:

- **The passage home from a site's pad, for the owner.** From a site's pad `+chart/ground` reads "no passage from <site>" for every other site and never shows the passage home on the port line, because site ports route only to the Freeport: a routing and text decision the owner holds (show the Freeport leg on the port line, or route site to site). Nothing is wrong in the data; the line is what the routes say.
- **The log pane holds the open excursion only, owner-visible.** A recover's tell writes `excursion: None`, so `projection_for` starts a clean log at the bay (D16); the pane empties when the rig comes home. Consistent with the projection rule; the owner may want the last excursion's log kept until the next start — SM.11's reconnect summary carries what a sleeping pilot missed either way.
- **The TUI steps rather than glides.** The TUI moves a rig only on its own paints (about every 4 s via the WHO reply); a smoother repaint needs a frame clock in `server.rs`, the owner's pixel file — not this train's to touch. The web repaints once a second while a leg is in flight.
- **Untested, residual.** The server-side gate emitting `rigs[].leg` only for an act on this site (a rig of the docked hull with an act on another site is unreachable in the test rig); `driving.rs` stays green.
- **Q8 in release, residual.** The Ceres frame with Ahuna's rows measured least 20.59 ms, median 21.98 ms in debug; the release run was not made (the brief's figure is a debug ceiling; SM.12's cost lane measures the feeds).

## SM.10

**Claims** (doc 20 §13's SM.10 row; §9 — D-20-12; §3.1's tenure words; §5's evidence rule): the block
record `tacsim.claims` (`BlockTenure { claim, paper }`) as the one public source of a block's
tenure, staged inside industry's own bundle while the epoch and the cooling rows stay industry's;
`+claim/stake|renew|release|contest|list` and `+registry <site>` as the player's own acts under the
site's issuer through industry's new `industry_claim_tenure` verb (`TenureKind::{Stake, Renew,
Lapse, Contest, Seed}`) and the composed `SurfaceTenure` authority — one act over the whole block
from a rig standing in it, an optional declared family, the fee per block; the hand-made evidence
rule (`evidence_at`: the earliest `Scan|Sound|QuietSound|Core` stamp `via: Hand` in the actor's own
rings, plus `first_local_at` while no `Plan` entry exists — a heard or plan-made reading never

a lapse by choice with the same cooling; a fee cancelled, amended or re-offered after landing lapsed

2026-10-22 on main from `16b0ca4e` (the Draft 0.10 docs commit `3af7f27b` landing under the run)
and rebased onto the owner's graphics cuts before the push. Judged **ship-with-notes**; the lead

### Deferred, and why

- **Lead rulings taken by the planner (brief §0, binding; recorded for the owner):** (1) a claim is one act over the whole block, the fee per block, nothing printed reads the deposit count; (2) the evidence rule reads the chart's provenance, hand-made only, from the stand; (3) fees are Public E4 contracts in `licence_spec`'s shape, lane v12 data; (4) the worked floor reads the cursors less tacsim's own `worked_at_term_start`; (5) lapses are the clerk's, one a fire, stamped at the term end; (6) release = a lapse by choice; (7) the take-over on re-stake; (8) the contest as a server-authored row on a loud heard sounding; (9) the interlock lever's `false` refused at config load; (10) Occator's holdings and the Syndicate paper seeded by the clerk from lane v12; (11) the Registrar's rule inside the player's renewal; (12) `site.claims` + `#`; (13) no RNG, no truth leak, lane v12. Decisions D1–D20 as the brief records them, including D18 (the contest window opens at the block's last opening, `opened_ic`), D19 (a fee cancelled after landing lapses unpaid; an expired one stands) and D20 (§9.2's "Transferable and pledgeable" yields to Bound; §9.6's "becomes Uncontested" yields to filed Uncontested).
- **Lead note 0a over §5 / §3.8 item 20** (the fixer's reading, accepted here): `+chart`'s `TENURE_LINE` and the ground chart's `tenure` now read `BlockTenure` and gain the word `{n} claimed` — one more owner-facing text under OC10.
- **Owner-critical defaults standing until the owner rules:** OC1 the fee arithmetic (stake 4,000 = 2,000 + 2,000; renewal 2,000; contest 4,000; refund 2,000); OC2 the Pallas Syndicate (a Ceres lane org, 50,000, faction `syndicate`) and its paper's adjudication contract (offered by the tick's GOD under the Syndicate's scope, adjudicated by `Party(Registry)`, a 5,000 bond never escrowed, a century's deadline, never accepted or ruled); OC3 seeded claims run a century; OC4 surface claims are `Bound`, no title; OC5 a papered block's player claim is filed Uncontested; OC6 release is a lapse by choice with cooling; OC7 the declared family as an optional word, public on the registry; OC8 stake from the ground only, contest from aboard the hull on the site; OC9 renewal at any time while live, from the term end; OC10 every new player-facing text (§3.10 verbatim, `WHICH_RIG_STAKE`, `CLAIM_WHICH`, `TENURE_SUMMARY`, the canon line "{holder}'s claim on block {L} at {site} lapsed." naming the holder in the chronicle, and the tenure word "{n} claimed"); OC11 tacsim's record staged inside industry's bundle; OC12 the heard count's 512-row bound and "at least" (the exact per-block heard log not built); OC13 the interlock's `false` refused at boot; OC14 a refused act's escrow held up to an hour; OC15 the cooling term binds the holder, anyone who acts for it and the holder's whole gateway account (staff refused too while any row is live); OC16 a fee cancelled, amended or re-offered after landing lapses the claim with cooling, an expired one stands and pages; OC17 the contest window opens at the block's last opening, never at a take-over or a transfer.
- **The fixer's owner question (correctness F5):** whether a contest whose fee is withdrawn after landing should restore the loser's claim. As built the block lapses unpaid, the contester cools, the loser is told CONTEST_LOST and gets their paid term fee back, and the block reopens.
- **Deviations accepted:** `BlockKey` key text lower-cases the letter; `TenureKind::Contest` carries `term_at` and `transfer_tenure_termed` sets the term in one post-image; `INDUSTRY_SEAMS` 9 → 12 (not 11); the claim handles from a lazy `OnceLock` in `SurfaceTenure`, not `with_claim_cell`; `claim_edges(&[char]) -> Vec`; `BlockPaper.suspended_ic`; `block_tenure_now` lives in `port::claims`, not `port::site`; the live-object check in `project_offer`; `world_with_table`/`remap` in `tests/claims.rs` not `support/`; `tests/mining.rs` not refactored onto the new support; C9's alt made by remapping the lapsed holder onto Alt's account and C10's race by `forget_claim_order_for_tests` (the licence is one holder an account, so no verb makes the alt); C20's Expired-fee contest case unreachable (CLAIM_PENDING bars it), the never-paid arm reached by a staff-hand record edit instead; STAKE_COMMONS unpinned (needs a pad at a commons site).
- **Not built:** the exact per-block heard log (D12's alternative, the owner's call); org-held claims, the frontier and the fight (§17), the Outer Claims front (doc 11), title deeds and `@claim/transfer`/pledge of surface claims, plan-made readings (`via: Plan`, SM.11 — which must revisit `evidence_at`'s `first_local_at` clause), Occator's drones and the mill (SM.12); the clients' rendering of `site.claims` beyond the grid's `#` (§5: no client change).
- **Residuals:** R1 (an expired-after-landing claim stands free and reads CLAIM_PENDING to all); R2 (the 512-row bound); R3 (the ring's four entries can evict a challenger's early loud sounding); R4 (the paper contract's re-find scans every contract while the log lacks the row); the LAPSED_TOLD re-tell after a lost claim log (conformance F9); the double revision bump on a contest (conformance F7); the two `#[doc(hidden)] pub` test helpers; `deploy/instance/mushd.toml.tmpl`'s five lines in the owner's area (the lead's call).

### Residual risks the judge named

- OC16/R1: a landed claim whose fee expired unaccepted (an outage past the real hour) stands free for its term and its holder and every rival read CLAIM_PENDING ('try again shortly') until the due lapse (conformance F5) — the owner's call on the Expired case.
- An unpaid contest (the fee cancelled, amended or re-offered after landing) lapses the block, cools the contester, tells the loser CONTEST_LOST and still refunds the loser's paid term fee from the Registry's account; the loser's claim is not restored (the fixer's owner question on correctness F5).
- deploy/instance/mushd.toml.tmpl gains five lines ([tacsim.surface] registry_interlock = true) in the owner's deploy/ area: the census test live_surface_interlock_is_true_in_every_shipped_config fails if it is reverted; the lead stages it or narrows the census to mushd.toml.example.
- After a lost claim log (Unreadable), item 4 re-chronicles nothing (records_for_source guards it) but re-tells LAPSED_TOLD/UNPAID_LAPSED to each lapsed holder once per block (conformance F9, unaddressed, cosmetic).
- transfer_tenure_termed bumps the claim revision twice in one post-image (transferred + with_term): harmless today (ClaimRev reads the current revision) but a contest moves the revision by 2 (conformance F7, unaddressed).
- R2/R3: the heard count's 512-row scan ('at least N', logged once a process via a static AtomicBool, not once a boot) and the provenance ring's four entries, which can evict a challenger's early loud sounding (heard_before reads the ring only; the holder's discovery survives by first_local_at).
- R4: the paper contract's re-find scans every contract in the economy snapshot, but only while the claim log lacks the row.
- A staff @claim-filed-then-lapsed claim on a block with no BlockTenure record plans a take-over (reopen = true) that stage's (None, true) arm refuses with 'That block is under claim.' — a staff-only edge no verb reaches.
- CLAIM_ORDER_TTL_IC_SECS 3,600 IC seconds is 150 real seconds at rate 24: an order the world task does not land inside that window is never offered and its fee waits out its hour to refund (C17's path); a `go` after an engine back-pressure drop can escrow a second fee while the first is held (unchanged, the licence's behaviour).
- The claims suite costs ~63 s (three-world boots in C2, C16, C23; real-cycle work of 100 t in C14a); deterministic, no wall clock, but on CI's critical path.
- The lazy OnceLock in SurfaceTenure is filled at the first next_tenure call; a prepare that somehow runs before any offer in the process refuses with the STAGE_DARK line (fail closed, logged) — unreachable on the offer route, which always projects first.
- forget_claim_order_for_tests and claim_order_for_tests are #[doc(hidden)] pub in crates/tacsim/src/port/claims.rs (production code); any crate could evict a claim order.

### The lead's fix round (before the commit)

Three items fixed in the lead's pre-commit round (run `wf_8c4e765c-f02`: a fixer, one reviewer over the fix delta only — no must-fix; its one should-fix re-fixed — then the gate, fourteen commands green on the first run with no flake): **the Expired fee** — `fee_unpaid` now tells `Withdrawn` (cancelled, draft, or offered on terms that no longer hold: D19, the holder cooled) from `Expired` (never accepted before its hour ran out: no cooling), the clerk lapses the expired case under the same `tacsim.claim.unpaid/{site}/{l}/{epoch}` receipt as kind `expired` with `cooling_until = at`, tells `EXPIRED_LAPSED` ("Your fee for block {block} at {site} lapsed unpaid, so the Registry lapses the claim; you may stake it again.") once, and the block reopens; for "no cooling" to mean none, industry's `TenureRecord::on_lapse` writes no cooling row when `cooling_until` is not after `at` (a row already run out read as live after a clock-generation change and barred the holder for ever in the test); `ClaimLog.unpaid` (the old page-once memo) is removed, pre-launch, no migration. The fixer found the economy's second Expired case by test: a fee the Registry accepted before an outage passed its deadline is forfeit TO the Registry (`Expiry::Forfeit`), so that claim is paid — `fee_forfeit(contract)` (`Expired` and fully accepted) now counts as paid in `fee_recorded`, `fee_unpaid`, `fee_paid` (which reads the contract, not the bare state), the refund step and both `CONTEST_LOST`/`CONTEST_LOST_UNPAID` choices (the reviewer's should-fix, re-fixed: a contest loser whose fee was forfeit across an outage is refunded and told `CONTEST_LOST`, pinned by C20d with the Registry's and the loser's postings); **the contest's revision** — `ClaimRecord::transferred_termed` sets the term in the transfer's own post-image, so a contest moves `ClaimRev` by one like every other write (pinned in industry's tests and C11); **the lapse told once** — item 4's tell rides the chronicle's own `records_for_source` guard, so after an unreadable claim log a holder or a contest loser is told nothing again (C20's new sibling with a `{schema: 99}` log across two reboots). New tests C20b, C20c, C20d, the lost-log test and industry's cooling-row and termed-transfer tests; no pin moved. The reviewer's notes: `fee_forfeit` reads `Expired` + fully accepted rather than the economy's full forfeit predicate (`on_expiry == Forfeit { to: the Registry }`, a bound contract, a qualifying hold) — the claim fee spec always sets that, so it is defence in depth, left as a residual; item 4 picks the told line from the fee's state at tell time rather than from the lapse that landed, so a fee withdrawn and then expired across two outages could be told the other line — cosmetic, residual; two comment-and-guard notes fixed by the lead at landing (the `lapse_act` doc now says no row is written, and `on_lapse`'s cross-generation pair is read as cooling, never as no row).

The lead's rulings on the judge's residuals and the round's review:

- **The Expired fee (R1 / OC16), ruled in the round.** A landed claim whose fee expired unaccepted — an outage past the fee's real hour, the escrow refunded — no longer stands free for its term with every reader on `CLAIM_PENDING`: the clerk lapses it unpaid at its next visit, without the cooling term (no fault of the holder's), and the block reopens; the holder may re-stake. `CLAIM_PENDING` stays for the live window before the fee settles.
- **An unpaid contest, for the owner.** A contest whose fee is cancelled, amended or re-offered after the transfer landed lapses the block, cools the contester, tells the loser `CONTEST_LOST` and still refunds the loser's paid term fee from the Registry's account; the loser's claim is not restored (the block reopens and the loser, uncooled, may re-stake). The fixer asked whether the loser's claim should be restored instead; the lead keeps the lapse as the default and records the question.
- **The deploy template.** `deploy/instance/mushd.toml.tmpl` gains the five-line `[tacsim.surface] registry_interlock = true` block in the owner's `deploy/` area because the `mush-config` census requires the key explicit in every shipped config; staged with the cut (SM.1 and A.6 edited the same file under their cuts). The graphics session's G.1b adds a `[pixel]` section to the same template after this cut lands.
- **Residuals handed on:** the heard count's 512-row scan ("at least N", logged once a process) and the provenance ring's four entries, which can evict a challenger's early loud sounding (`heard_before` reads the ring only; the holder's discovery survives by `first_local_at`) — the exact per-block heard log is D12's alternative, the owner's call; the paper contract's re-find scanning every contract while the claim log lacks the row; a staff `@claim`-filed-then-lapsed claim on a block with no record refusing "under claim" (staff-only, no verb reaches it); `CLAIM_ORDER_TTL_IC_SECS` 3,600 IC s = 150 real s at rate 24, so an order the world task does not land in that window is never offered and its fee waits out its hour to refund, and a `go` after an engine back-pressure drop can escrow a second fee while the first is held (the licence's behaviour, unchanged); the claims suite's ~63 s on CI's critical path; the lazy `OnceLock` in `SurfaceTenure` refusing fail-closed if a prepare ever ran before any offer (unreachable on the offer route); `forget_claim_order_for_tests` / `claim_order_for_tests` as `#[doc(hidden)] pub` in production code (SM.8's `unload_order_for_tests` precedent).
- **An expired-unaccepted RENEWAL fee, for the owner (the round's review, F6).** The stage's Renew arm moves `term_end_ic` forward and points `claim.fee` at the renewal fee before that fee is paid; if a renewal fee expires unaccepted across an outage (several fees queued, the clerk accepting one a fire while the economy's sweep expires the rest), the clerk lapses the whole claim as unpaid — without cooling, by this round's rule, but the holder then needs a fresh hand reading to re-stake (the lapse opens a new epoch). The lead records the question: should an unpaid renewal instead revert the term to the paid term's end and leave the claim standing? The default stands until the owner rules; a small claims follow-up pins the renewal case either way.
- **A re-stake after an expired lapse needs a fresh reading, residual.** The evidence rule is unchanged, so the `EXPIRED_LAPSED` line's "you may stake it again" is true only after a new hand-made reading in the new epoch.
- **For SM.11:** `evidence_at`'s `first_local_at` clause trusts a ring with no `Plan` entry — SM.11 must revisit it once `via: Plan` stamps exist (a plan-made reading never qualifies a stake); `heard_count`/`heard_before` read the pocket ring only.

R1 / OC16: a landed claim whose fee expired unaccepted** — fixed: crates/tacsim/src/port/claims.rs: `fee_withdrawn` is replaced by `fee_unpaid(w, claim, registry) -> Option<FeeUnpaid>`. `FeeUnpaid` is a pub(crate) enum with two values. Withdrawn covers Cancelled, Draft, and an Offered fee whose terms no longer hold (D19, cools the holder). Expired covers a fee that expired before the Registry accepted it (no cooling). There is a new `fee_forfeit(contract)` = `state == Expired && contract.fully_accepted()`. The case it covers: the Registry accepted the fee, then an outage passed the deadline, so the economy's Expiry::Forfeit paid the escrow to the Registry. That claim is PAID: `fee_unpaid` returns None for it, and `fee_recorded` now counts it, so the claim's acts never answer CLAIM_PENDING because of it. I found this case empirically. A one-leap outage in the rig lets the clerk accept before the economy's expiry runs, and the Registry gains 4,000.00cr. Without this check the ruling would have lapsed a paid claim. The lead's ruling names only the unaccepted case, so I read this as following it, not as a new design. New text constant `EXPIRED_LAPSED` = "Your fee for block {block} at {site} lapsed unpaid, so the Registry lapses the claim; you may stake it again." (a sibling of UNPAID_LAPSED, in the voice the lead asked for). The tenure game kind `expired` was added to `TenureGame.kind` and to stage's Lapse arm.

crates/tacsim/src/port/site.rs: in `next_system_act`, item 2 lapses Withdrawn as kind `unpaid` with cooling, and Expired as kind `expired` with `cooling_until = at`. Both use the receipt `tacsim.claim.unpaid/{site}/{l}/{epoch}`: a fee has one state, so one lapse lands. `lapse_act` takes a `cools` flag. In `claims_step`, item 2 submits either kind. The old page-once loop for Expired is gone. Item 4 tells UNPAID_LAPSED, EXPIRED_LAPSED or LAPSED_TOLD by cause. A contest loser is told for either unpaid cause. The doc comments for items 2 and 4 and for `next_system_act` are rewritten.

crates/mush-industry (needed so that "no cooling term" really is none): `TenureRecord::on_lapse` now writes NO cooling row when `cooling_until` is not after `at`. The first cut wrote a row that had already run out. After any world-rate change, a new clock generation reads such a row as live (fail closed), and the C20b test showed the holder barred for ever. The `TenureKind::Lapse` doc in seams.rs states the rule. An earlier live row of the holder is kept, never shortened.

**The round's review.** Reviewed the delta from b29c9ca5 to the new tree 688993fdc4831d04cd5f9074636869fda5021172, which I recomputed with a scratch index and which matches the fixer's tree. It touches 8 files, adding 635 lines and removing 146. All three items are done correctly, each with a test that would fail without the fix. No existing assertion was weakened (the test diffs only add assertions), no pin moved, nothing leaks, there is no RNG, and there are no new refusals.

Item 1 (R1/OC16): `fee_unpaid` returns Withdrawn or Expired. The clerk lapses an Expired-unaccepted fee under the unpaid receipt as kind `expired` with `cools=false`. The stage's Lapse arm accepts the new kind, and players cannot reach it: it is offered only through `next_system_act` in the composed authority. The new line EXPIRED_LAPSED is told once. For "no cooling" to really mean no cooling, industry's `on_lapse` had to stop writing a row that runs out the instant it is written; such a row would bar the holder for ever after a clock-generation change. C20b reaches the state through the never-paid arm's seams (a market-clock expiry plus a staff `put_block`) and is discriminating: it pins CLAIM_PENDING before the clerk's visit, the clerk's unpaid receipt and nothing else, the line told once, epoch 1, no cooling rows, no money moved, and a re-stake after a clock-generation change.

Item 2 (F7): `ClaimRecord::transferred_termed` makes the change one post-image and one revision. It is pinned in mush-industry (the contest row +1, plus a new termed/plain/stale unit test) and in tacsim C11, where each claim's revision moves +1.

Item 3 (F9): item 4's `records_for_source` guard now skips the tell, the contest-loser tell included. The Unreadable path is forced by corrupting the stored log and rebooting. The test counts zero re-tells over many fires and a second reboot, and finds the log row restored.

One should-fix: the fixer's own extension, treating a fee forfeit to the Registry as paid, is applied in only two of the four places. `fee_recorded` now lets a contest go ahead on a forfeit-fee claim, which before this round answered CLAIM_PENDING. But `fee_paid` and item 3's refund match still treat the forfeit as never paid. The contest loser therefore loses their paid term fee and is told CONTEST_LOST_UNPAID. That money loss for the player is a path this fix newly opened.

The notes cover:
- `fee_forfeit` only approximates the economy's forfeit rule.
- A stale `lapse_act` doc comment.
- `on_lapse` failing open on a cross-generation stamp pair.
- The item-4 told line chosen from the fee's state at tell time rather than from the lapse that landed.
- A question for the lead: an expired-unaccepted renewal fee lapses the whole claim, losing the rest of the already-paid term.

The fixer's decision to treat a forfeit as paid goes beyond the lead's list and needs the lead's ratification.

- **F1** (should-fix): The fix makes a forfeit fee (Expired and fully_accepted) count as paid in only two of the places that ask whether a fee was paid. `fee_recorded` (crates/tacsim/src/port/claims.rs:590-603) and `fee_unpaid` (claims.rs:579) count it as paid. `fee_paid` (site.rs:1558-1567), the refund match in claims_step item 3 (site.rs:1949-1958) and the CONTEST_LOST/CONTEST_LOST_UNPAID choice (site.rs:1888 and 2074) still count only Active, ReadyToSettle or Settled. Before this round, an Expired holder fee made `fee_recorded` false, so `plan_contest`'s gate (claims.rs:1585) answered CLAIM_PENDING and nobody could contest that claim. Now `fee_recorded` is true, so the contest goes ahead. The stage's Contest arm writes `RefundOwed { paid_by: old.fee }` (claims.rs:~2728). Item 3 then sends the forfeit `paid_by` to its `_ => "The loser never paid: nothing is owed"` arm and logs the refund as done, and item 1 tells the loser CONTEST_LOST_UNPAID. The loser paid the term fee, the Registry holds it through the forfeit, and the loser never gets it back. The fix opened this path; it did not exist before. The fixer's note 3 calls it pre-existing, which it is not.
- **F2** (note): claims.rs:551-553: `fee_forfeit` = `state == Expired && fully_accepted()`, and its doc calls this the economy's own rule. The economy's actual rule (crates/mush-economy/src/contract_live.rs:3880-3915) forfeits only when `on_expiry` is Forfeit, the contract is bound (fully accepted and more than one party) and the escrow has a qualifying hold. A bound contract with no qualifying escrow is unwound to Expired as a refund, and its acceptances stay intact, so `fully_accepted()` still reads true. Today the two rules give the same answer, because item 1 accepts only fees that pass `fee_terms_hold`: Forfeit to the Registry, two parties, escrow taken at offer. But the check reads the economy's outcome from indirect signals, not from a record of what happened. The fixer's decision to treat a forfeit as paid also goes beyond the lead's list; the lead should ratify it (fixer's note 1).
- **F3** (note): site.rs:1478-1482: the `lapse_act` doc says the no-cooling lapse cools "to `at` itself, a row that has run out the instant it is written". After the same round's change to mush-industry (`TenureRecord::on_lapse`, record.rs:1552 and its doc at 1527-1532), no row is written at all, and that doc says so explicitly. The comment now describes the behaviour the fixer had to remove, the one that barred the holder for ever across a clock generation.
- **F4** (note): record.rs:1552: `let cools = matches!(at.checked_cmp(cooling_until), Ok(Less));` returns false when the two stamps come from different clock generations (Err), so no row is written. That fails open, while the rest of `on_lapse` fails closed across generations ("across generations it is kept"). The provider stamps both values with the same `stamp()` (provider.rs:2663), so the act path cannot reach this. The public `IndustryFamilies::tenure_lapse` and `lapse_claim` accept any pair of stamps. The new unit test `sm10_a_lapse_cooling_to_its_own_instant_cools_nobody` covers only `cooling_until == at`.
- **F5** (note): Item 4 (site.rs:2065-2096) picks the told line by calling `claims::fee_unpaid` at tell time. It does not use the lapse that actually landed. Item 2 submitted a cooling or a non-cooling lapse from the fee's state one or more fires earlier. Suppose a fee re-offered on other terms (Withdrawn, so the holder is cooled) expires unaccepted across an outage between that lapse landing and the chronicle step. The holder is then told EXPIRED_LAPSED ("you may stake it again") while their cooling row is live. The opposite mismatch is the fixer's note 5: an amended or re-offered fee that expires before the clerk's fire reads Expired at claims.rs:579 and lapses with no cooling.
- **F6** (note): The stage's Renew arm (claims.rs:2678-2689) moves `term_end_ic` forward and sets `claim.fee = game.contract` to the renewal fee before that fee is paid. Suppose a renewal fee expires unaccepted across an outage, for example when several fees are queued and the clerk accepts one per fire while the economy's sweep expires the rest. Item 2 (site.rs:1613-1632) then lapses the whole claim at once. The holder loses the rest of the term the earlier, settled fee already paid for, "no fault of the holder's". This follows the lead's ruling to the letter ("exactly as D19"), but C20b pins only the stake case. Separately, EXPIRED_LAPSED's "you may stake it again" needs a fresh hand reading, because the lapse opens a new epoch (the fixer's note 4).

**Re-fixed after the review:**

- **F1** — fixed: Fixed by the first option the reviewer offered: a forfeit fee now counts as paid everywhere. The reviewer is right that my lead-round change opened this path, and I withdraw note 3 calling it pre-existing. In crates/tacsim/src/port/site.rs, `fee_paid` now takes `(&World, id)` and reads the contract instead of the bare state. It returns `fee_settled(w, id) || state is Active|ReadyToSettle`. The new `fee_settled(w, id)` is true for `Settled` or `crate::port::claims::fee_forfeit(contract)`. Both CONTEST_LOST/CONTEST_LOST_UNPAID choices (item 1 and the item 4 chronicle tell) call the new `fee_paid`. Item 3's refund match gains a first arm, `_ if fee_settled(ctx.w, refund.paid_by) => {}`, so a forfeit `paid_by` goes to the paying path and no longer reaches the 'never paid' arm. The four places now agree with `claims::fee_recorded` and `claims::fee_unpaid`. New sibling test C20d, `sm10_a_fee_forfeit_to_the_registry_is_refunded_when_contested` in crates/tacsim/tests/claims.rs, with a helper `refund_posts` that filters the economy's transactions by cause Internal kind == CLAIM_REFUND_KEY. Steps: Bryn sounds loudly, Ada stakes, the outage forfeits her accepted fee, and the claim stands. Bryn's contest then lands, and the refund owed is (Ada, Ada's forfeit fee). Assertions: Ada hears CONTEST_LOST and never CONTEST_LOST_UNPAID. Exactly one CLAIM_REFUND_KEY transaction, whose lines are {Registry: -200_000, Ada: +200_000}. Ada's available balance rises by exactly term_minor. The Registry's balance equals before + Bryn's escrowed fee - term_minor. After a reboot and five more fires, nothing is posted twice. I checked that the test catches the bug: with the forfeit arm of `fee_settled` disabled, it fails at the CONTEST_LOST assertion, the loser having heard the _UNPAID line. I restored the code after that run. No existing test was weakened.
